civility.explanation: Opposes the bill while repeatedly thanking the member and engaging respectfully with the arguments for it.

civility.statement: A lot of those members opposite know where their bread is buttered and their consciences will subsequently fall into line because they know that this is very popular within the public and within small business
civility.explanation: A cynical characterisation of opponents' motives, delivered light-heartedly but still a swipe.

civility.statement: Mr Parker can heckle all he wants, but he will be the first chardonnay socialist, turning up on his bike with his leg in a cast, on two crutches, with his $5, pulling in for a $10 pinot noir tasting, somewhere out the back of Bannockburn, telling them that he voted for this bill
civility.explanation: A jocular personal caricature of a colleague ('chardonnay socialist'); teasing in tone but a personal jab rather than substance.

authenticity.statement: But I do want law which works, that's good, and that's consistent and that's fair, and this isn't it.
authenticity.explanation: States a consistent principle (support well-framed, even-handed law) that aligns with his stated willingness to back a better bill; a defensible position rather than a demonstrated record match.

authenticity.statement: it's really important that I express the views of my community, Māngere, in South Auckland, where, obviously, we have got some challenges in our local community. … The main reason that I am against this bill is that I asked that the definitions would be very clear … Those are the views that I wanted to put across, and I won't be supporting this bill.
authenticity.explanation: States a consistent, principled position rooted in her community's alcohol-harm concerns and votes accordingly, matching words to her stated stance despite thanking the member.

forthrightness.statement: Well, I think we have done a lot as a Government to remove barriers, and I'm proud to be supporting a member's bill that would do the same. … Things that remove barriers to trade, such as repealing the restrictions around Easter trading, would be a huge addition to the sectors that need this
forthrightness.explanation: In response to Meager's question 'What other changes could we make to remove barriers?', he does name a concrete example (Easter trading) but frames it around his own talking point rather than the bill's subject.

divination.statement: We've also heard that this industry is a $2.4 billion industry. But, as I said in my second reading speech on this bill, that's fast-approaching to be a $3 billion industry and is growing.
divination.explanation: Predicts the industry is 'fast-approaching' $3 billion — plausible given a growing sector but no timeframe given, so weakly checkable.

veracity.statement: This Government is implementing a more proactive welfare system to support New Zealanders into work, because in the six years before we came to office the number of people receiving the jobseeker benefit increased by 70,000, or 57 percent. For part of these six years, businesses were desperate for staff, which underscores why the welfare system needs to do more to support job seekers into work.
veracity.explanation: Jobseeker numbers did rise substantially over 2017-2023; the 70,000/57% figure is broadly in range, though 'businesses desperate for staff' is a selective framing.

veracity.statement: What we do know from what we have inherited over the last six years: the number of job seekers increased by 70,000; the number of children living in benefit-dependent households increased by 44,000. So now there are one in five New Zealand children growing up in a benefit-dependent household.
veracity.explanation: Broadly consistent with reported trends, but 'inherited' framing avoids the numbers under her own tenure that were asked about.

veracity.statement: Young people who go on to jobseeker benefit under the age of 25 are currently predicted to spend nearly two decades of their lives on welfare.
veracity.explanation: Reflects a real modelled estimate but is presented as settled fact without its considerable uncertainty.

veracity.statement: incomes rise over time due to inflation and growth in the economy, but if tax rates and thresholds remain the same, more and more of people's incomes are taxed at higher marginal rates, and they will pay a higher and higher proportion of their income in tax.
veracity.explanation: Accurate description of how unindexed thresholds interact with rising nominal incomes.

veracity.statement: every Government since 1980, whether National-led or Labour-led, has, at some stage, adjusted rates or thresholds to provide tax relief to hard-working New Zealanders—oh, with one solitary exception. The solitary exception is the previous Labour Government.
veracity.explanation: Broadly defensible historically but delivered as a rhetorical 'gotcha' that glosses over Labour's other tax changes.

veracity.statement: I am advised that as of this morning, 638,000 people have used the tax calculator to see what they are getting in long overdue tax relief. That is 39,000 more people than yesterday, and 121,000 more than this time last week.
veracity.explanation: Attributed usage statistics ('I am advised'), plausible but unverifiable from the text.

veracity.statement: yes, in context. That context was a botched merger of district health boards (DHBs) where national planning and budgeting was disconnected from local management, where financial reporting was ineffective, where data systems were fragmented, and where, in consequence, there was limited oversight of financial performance.
veracity.explanation: The organisational problems cited are widely reported, though 'botched' is a loaded characterisation.

veracity.statement: Oranga Tamariki was reviewing its costs and efficiencies long before this Government directed the Public Service to make any savings. The proposed organisational restructure has not just been about making cuts or finding savings. This is part of Oranga Tamariki's journey to become an effective statutory care and protection agency that's focused on its core responsibilities.
veracity.explanation: Plausible but unverifiable from the text and framed to distance the restructure from Budget savings.

veracity.statement: In June alone, Health New Zealand has advised that over 883 people were hired, including 124 doctors, 243 nurses, 30 midwives, and 140 allied health professionals. That doesn't sound like a hiring freeze to me.
veracity.explanation: Attributed hiring figures; plausible but selectively rebuts 'hiring freeze' by counting gross clinical hires, not net or clerical roles.

veracity.statement: There are 137 investments in planning, with an estimated value of $93.7 billion, and 171 investments in delivery, with a combined approved budget of $79.4 billion.
veracity.explanation: Cites figures from the report he released; plausible but unverifiable here.

veracity.statement: the characterisation of a form letter sent to hundreds of people and organisations as an invitation is wrong. It was not an invitation; it was basically a form letter to say the fast-track process is happening.
veracity.explanation: Disputes the 'invitation' label; a contested characterisation where the letter did solicit applications, so the distinction is partly semantic.

veracity.statement: those matters really fall within the remit and the purview of operations rather than the Minister, and I'll leave those for the ministry. However, I will note that in Budget 2024, 19 kura have been supported for renovation.
veracity.explanation: A checkable Budget claim, plausible but unverified here and not addressing the 15 halted programmes asked about.

veracity.statement: One recent IPCA inquiry found that police officers were illegally taking photos and storing thousands of photos of young Māori on their phones, and this really adds to this reality that there are some communities that are more heavily surveilled and have more frequent interactions with police.
veracity.explanation: Refers to a real IPCA finding on unlawful photographing of rangatahi; broadly accurate, though 'thousands' is a summarised figure.

veracity.statement: my colleague Kahurangi Carter made the comment that many New Zealanders would rather walk down a dark alleyway with a patched gang member than with a police officer, and this caused some disagreement from the Minister. But the reality is that this is a statement of fact and that is how some people feel.
veracity.explanation: Labels a subjective sentiment 'a statement of fact'; that some people feel this way may be true, but 'many' and the claim's factual status are overstated.

specificity.statement: This Government is implementing a more proactive welfare system to support New Zealanders into work, because in the six years before we came to office the number of people receiving the jobseeker benefit increased by 70,000, or 57 percent. For part of these six years, businesses were desperate for staff, which underscores why the welfare system needs to do more to support job seekers into work.
specificity.explanation: Cites concrete figures (70,000, 57%) and a named benefit and timeframe.

specificity.statement: What we do know from what we have inherited over the last six years: the number of job seekers increased by 70,000; the number of children living in benefit-dependent households increased by 44,000. So now there are one in five New Zealand children growing up in a benefit-dependent household.
specificity.explanation: Concrete figures (70,000, 44,000, one in five).

specificity.statement: Today, I announced that 2,100 extra places will be available in community-led programmes in the 2024-25 financial year to help those on jobseeker benefits, aged 18 to 24, shift into work as part of year one of Welfare that Works.
specificity.explanation: Names the number of places, the age band, the financial year, and the named programme.

specificity.statement: incomes rise over time due to inflation and growth in the economy, but if tax rates and thresholds remain the same, more and more of people's incomes are taxed at higher marginal rates, and they will pay a higher and higher proportion of their income in tax.
specificity.explanation: Explains the mechanism clearly but without figures until the minimum-wage example.

specificity.statement: I am advised that as of this morning, 638,000 people have used the tax calculator to see what they are getting in long overdue tax relief. That is 39,000 more people than yesterday, and 121,000 more than this time last week.
specificity.explanation: Precise figures with day-on-day and week-on-week comparisons.

specificity.statement: In June alone, Health New Zealand has advised that over 883 people were hired, including 124 doctors, 243 nurses, 30 midwives, and 140 allied health professionals. That doesn't sound like a hiring freeze to me.
specificity.explanation: Breaks the figure down by role type over a defined month.

specificity.statement: What I acknowledge is that we are committed to reconnecting with the clinical front line and delivering better patient outcomes.
specificity.explanation: Vague aspiration ('reconnecting', 'better outcomes') with no mechanism.

specificity.statement: This morning, I announced that the Government is going to release quarterly investment reports which outline information on large Government investments throughout their life. This is part of our plan to get the books back in order, drive better performance from agencies, and also give New Zealanders the openness and transparency they deserve about their investments.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete new mechanism (quarterly investment reports) but describes its purpose in general terms.

specificity.statement: There are 137 investments in planning, with an estimated value of $93.7 billion, and 171 investments in delivery, with a combined approved budget of $79.4 billion.
specificity.explanation: Precise counts and dollar values for both pipeline stages.

specificity.statement: There are many. At the expert panel stage of the process, conditions will be set to protect the environment. As the bill is currently drafted, in deciding whether a project is eligible to be referred to a panel, Ministers may consider whether the project will address significant environmental issues. Ministers may decline an application if Ministers consider the project may have significant adverse effects on the environment. Applications will include an assessment of environmental effects, with an assessment against relevant national direction, regional, and district planning documents. The member should read the bill.
specificity.explanation: Enumerates concrete bill mechanisms (panel conditions, ministerial decline power, assessments).

specificity.statement: it's got to be a fast-track process because it's too hard to do things in this country—it takes too long and costs too much. And it has to be a one-stop-shop regime because that's a core part of the regime.
specificity.explanation: States the design principle (fast-track, one-stop-shop) but not the concrete parameters.

specificity.statement: 132 events across the motu will receive a funding boost through the Regional Events Promotion Fund. The Regional Events Promotion Fund was established using $5 million of the international visitor levy revenue and supports the promotion of regional tourism organisations and local councils outside the main centres to attract more New Zealanders to their events throughout the year. The first round of the fund has resulted in funding for a total of 132 events, to the value of $2.3 million.
specificity.explanation: Names event count, fund size, funding source, and total value awarded.

specificity.statement: Heaps of value. This fund will help promote regional events that will deliver a high return on investment and encourage visitors to explore beyond the main centres. There is life in New Zealand outside the big cities.
specificity.explanation: Vague benefits ('heaps of value', 'high return on investment') with no figures or measures.

specificity.statement: In terms of the confusion around numbers, we clarified the system to ensure there was total clarity so that when we reach 2,711, we will have increased the police force by 500, as New Zealand First and National committed to do.
specificity.explanation: Ties the '500 more police' commitment to a concrete target headcount (2,711).

specificity.statement: those matters really fall within the remit and the purview of operations rather than the Minister, and I'll leave those for the ministry. However, I will note that in Budget 2024, 19 kura have been supported for renovation.
specificity.explanation: Provides a concrete figure (19 kura supported in Budget 2024).

specificity.statement: One recent IPCA inquiry found that police officers were illegally taking photos and storing thousands of photos of young Māori on their phones, and this really adds to this reality that there are some communities that are more heavily surveilled and have more frequent interactions with police.
specificity.explanation: Cites a concrete inquiry finding to support the point.

rigor.statement: This Government is implementing a more proactive welfare system to support New Zealanders into work, because in the six years before we came to office the number of people receiving the jobseeker benefit increased by 70,000, or 57 percent. For part of these six years, businesses were desperate for staff, which underscores why the welfare system needs to do more to support job seekers into work.
rigor.explanation: Uses data but implies the rise was a failure of the welfare system rather than of the economic cycle — a gap in causal reasoning.

rigor.statement: I'm very proud of Budget 2024, of tax relief, of focusing on the cost of living because the cost of living crisis is the single biggest impact on the number of children living in poverty today. That's why our side of the House is unwilling to tolerate that level of hardship.
rigor.explanation: Asserts the cost-of-living crisis is 'the single biggest impact' without evidence, sidestepping the specific indexing/benefit changes raised.

rigor.statement: incomes rise over time due to inflation and growth in the economy, but if tax rates and thresholds remain the same, more and more of people's incomes are taxed at higher marginal rates, and they will pay a higher and higher proportion of their income in tax.
rigor.explanation: A correct, well-structured explanation of fiscal drag / bracket creep with the conclusion following from the premise.

rigor.statement: yes, in context. That context was a botched merger of district health boards (DHBs) where national planning and budgeting was disconnected from local management, where financial reporting was ineffective, where data systems were fragmented, and where, in consequence, there was limited oversight of financial performance.
rigor.explanation: Marshals several specific structural claims to support the 'didn't know what questions to ask' characterisation.

rigor.statement: What I would say is stakeholder groups, Opposition parties, Governments, and Māori have all called for Oranga Tamariki to change. This is what change looks like. It's not an option to keep the status quo. To do so would be to say we're happy with how the organisation is running now and delivering for children, and we know it's not. So I would urge the Opposition to get on board and make sure that we can enable change that's going to be enduring.
rigor.explanation: Leans on a false dichotomy (this restructure or endorsing the status quo) rather than engaging the specific harms raised.

rigor.statement: In June alone, Health New Zealand has advised that over 883 people were hired, including 124 doctors, 243 nurses, 30 midwives, and 140 allied health professionals. That doesn't sound like a hiring freeze to me.
rigor.explanation: Evidence-backed rebuttal, though it answers the 'freeze' framing while sidestepping the specific clerical-staffing concern.

rigor.statement: We have inherited a system that cares a lot about paying consultants to write business cases and not enough about delivering and looking after the investments that we already have and that we need.
rigor.explanation: A rhetorical characterisation ('cares about consultants not delivery') asserted rather than evidenced.

rigor.statement: it's got to be a fast-track process because it's too hard to do things in this country—it takes too long and costs too much. And it has to be a one-stop-shop regime because that's a core part of the regime.
rigor.explanation: Asserts consenting is 'too hard/too long/too costly' as self-evident justification without supporting evidence.

rigor.statement: if it's a quote, it should be in quotes so that we can, therefore, check against the evidence to see whether it's honestly reported or not. If it doesn't have any quote marks to it, no one knows what's going on here, and with the greatest respect to the Clerk of the House, if this was a court of law, they'd ask for that as well.
rigor.explanation: A coherent procedural argument that verifiable quotation requires quotation marks, though the court-of-law analogy is an appeal to analogy.

rigor.statement: given that the National Party brought in kura kaupapa Māori, why is he now being lectured on it?
rigor.explanation: A rhetorical 'who are you to lecture us' framing that appeals to origin rather than engaging the report's substance.

rigor.statement: One recent IPCA inquiry found that police officers were illegally taking photos and storing thousands of photos of young Māori on their phones, and this really adds to this reality that there are some communities that are more heavily surveilled and have more frequent interactions with police.
rigor.explanation: Uses a documented finding as evidence for the differential-policing claim.

rigor.statement: my colleague Kahurangi Carter made the comment that many New Zealanders would rather walk down a dark alleyway with a patched gang member than with a police officer, and this caused some disagreement from the Minister. But the reality is that this is a statement of fact and that is how some people feel.
rigor.explanation: Defends a provocative claim by asserting it is fact ('that is how some people feel') rather than evidencing the 'many'.

rigor.statement: in the small town that I grew up in in Tokoroa, it was a common occurrence to have breath checks on our main road every week, and I was pulled over multiple times as a young person... but I've never been pulled up in Wellington. There's a huge difference between the way that some communities, particularly those with low socio-economic indicators and those that are predominantly Māori or Pacific, are more heavily policed than other communities.
rigor.explanation: Generalises from personal anecdote to a systemic claim; the broader point is plausible but the evidence offered is a single lived example.

forthrightness.statement: What we do know from what we have inherited over the last six years: the number of job seekers increased by 70,000; the number of children living in benefit-dependent households increased by 44,000. So now there are one in five New Zealand children growing up in a benefit-dependent household.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether the extra 21,000 people on benefits since she took office would increase child poverty, she pivots to figures about the previous government rather than her own record.

forthrightness.statement: As that member has asked before and we have traversed, changes around tax and tax refunds are the responsibility of the Minister of Revenue.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to confirm specific Treasury advice that 9,000 beneficiaries would be worse off, she deflects to another Minister's portfolio rather than confirm or deny.

forthrightness.statement: I'm very proud of Budget 2024, of tax relief, of focusing on the cost of living because the cost of living crisis is the single biggest impact on the number of children living in poverty today. That's why our side of the House is unwilling to tolerate that level of hardship.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked why she won't admit her decisions increase child poverty, she pivots to pride in the Budget and general cost-of-living talking points.

forthrightness.statement: Because I did not entirely agree with the characterisations in the letter, and the comments I made in my letter were consistent with the advice I received from my officials.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly answers why she made the comments despite the board's rejection — she disagreed and relied on official advice.

forthrightness.statement: Yes, in the context in which I said it, which was in relation to the proposed Oranga Tamariki organisational restructure. From the beginning, the safety of children has been at the forefront of all decision making about the proposed restructure, and front-line managers and staff who report to them have been out of scope of this process. However, I do recognise that this has been an unsettling time for all staff at Oranga Tamariki, front-line or otherwise, and I just want to take the opportunity to acknowledge this.
forthrightness.explanation: Stands by the quoted guarantee but narrows it to the restructure; still acknowledges the question's premise.

forthrightness.statement: I'll say it again: the member is conflating two issues. My statement was in relation to the Oranga Tamariki restructure.
forthrightness.explanation: Repeated verbatim across several distinct supplementary questions (Māngere East layoffs, NZCCSS service gaps, the Malachi Subecz report) as a blanket non-answer.

forthrightness.statement: Oranga Tamariki was reviewing its costs and efficiencies long before this Government directed the Public Service to make any savings. The proposed organisational restructure has not just been about making cuts or finding savings. This is part of Oranga Tamariki's journey to become an effective statutory care and protection agency that's focused on its core responsibilities.
forthrightness.explanation: Partly engages the 'broken promise/budget cuts' charge but reframes it as a pre-existing reform rather than answering the funding-cut impact.

forthrightness.statement: What I acknowledge is that we are committed to reconnecting with the clinical front line and delivering better patient outcomes.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to acknowledge that cutting clerical jobs leaves doctors doing admin, he retreats to a general commitment slogan.

forthrightness.statement: Because the patients have also seen the layers and layers of management that that Government put in as part of their botched health reforms, and we're reconnecting the front line.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked why the public should believe him over front-line doctors and nurses, he redirects to attacking the previous government's reforms.

forthrightness.statement: Yes, and yes.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly and unambiguously affirms both parts of the question about protections for the taiao in the Fast-track Bill.

forthrightness.statement: There are many. At the expert panel stage of the process, conditions will be set to protect the environment. As the bill is currently drafted, in deciding whether a project is eligible to be referred to a panel, Ministers may consider whether the project will address significant environmental issues. Ministers may decline an application if Ministers consider the project may have significant adverse effects on the environment. Applications will include an assessment of environmental effects, with an assessment against relevant national direction, regional, and district planning documents. The member should read the bill.
forthrightness.explanation: Lists specific protection mechanisms in answer to what they are, though he doesn't directly address the water-conservation-order override raised.

forthrightness.statement: the characterisation of a form letter sent to hundreds of people and organisations as an invitation is wrong. It was not an invitation; it was basically a form letter to say the fast-track process is happening.
forthrightness.explanation: Answers the 'message to Save Our Springs' question by disputing its premise rather than addressing the group's concern.

forthrightness.statement: The Hon Dr Nick Smith is a friend and someone who I have a lot of time and respect for. I haven't seen those full comments and I haven't seen them in their full context, so it's difficult to proffer a view without that.
forthrightness.explanation: Declines to engage the substance of Nick Smith's quoted view on water conservation orders, citing lack of context.

forthrightness.statement: As I've clarified, there is no counting in different ways. We have clarified. But what I would say that is important to police morale is that we are getting tough on crime, and we are making police able to do their job... We are not the Government that will be soft on gangs. We will support the morale of the police and allow them to get back to catching the bad guys.
forthrightness.explanation: Denies the 'different ways to count' premise then pivots to tough-on-crime talking points rather than the morale question asked.

forthrightness.statement: those matters really fall within the remit and the purview of operations rather than the Minister, and I'll leave those for the ministry. However, I will note that in Budget 2024, 19 kura have been supported for renovation.
forthrightness.explanation: Declines to commit on reinstating the 15 stopped building programmes, deferring to 'operations', but offers one concrete counter-fact.

strength.statement: Today, I announced that 2,100 extra places will be available in community-led programmes in the 2024-25 financial year to help those on jobseeker benefits, aged 18 to 24, shift into work as part of year one of Welfare that Works.
strength.explanation: A concrete, funded commitment being rolled out, though delivery/outcomes are still prospective (an announcement of year one).

strength.statement: This morning, I announced that the Government is going to release quarterly investment reports which outline information on large Government investments throughout their life. This is part of our plan to get the books back in order, drive better performance from agencies, and also give New Zealanders the openness and transparency they deserve about their investments.
strength.explanation: An announced-and-delivered reporting change, though impact on 'performance' is prospective.

strength.statement: 132 events across the motu will receive a funding boost through the Regional Events Promotion Fund. The Regional Events Promotion Fund was established using $5 million of the international visitor levy revenue and supports the promotion of regional tourism organisations and local councils outside the main centres to attract more New Zealanders to their events throughout the year. The first round of the fund has resulted in funding for a total of 132 events, to the value of $2.3 million.
strength.explanation: A coalition-agreement commitment being delivered with concrete disbursements, though outcomes are yet to be seen.

strength.statement: In terms of the confusion around numbers, we clarified the system to ensure there was total clarity so that when we reach 2,711, we will have increased the police force by 500, as New Zealand First and National committed to do.
strength.explanation: Restates the commitment with a target but recruitment is behind (124 after eight months, per the questioner), so delivery is unproven.

divination.statement: Young people who go on to jobseeker benefit under the age of 25 are currently predicted to spend nearly two decades of their lives on welfare.
divination.explanation: A long-range projection of lifetime welfare dependency; directionally supported by actuarial modelling but the '~two decades' magnitude is uncertain and depends on assumptions.

charisma.statement: every Government since 1980, whether National-led or Labour-led, has, at some stage, adjusted rates or thresholds to provide tax relief to hard-working New Zealanders—oh, with one solitary exception. The solitary exception is the previous Labour Government.
charisma.explanation: Rhetorically effective but purely a partisan jab at the opposition, not consensus-building.

charisma.statement: I am not advised as to how many of them were Labour voters, but I'm guessing some. Let us not forget that members opposite voted against it.
charisma.explanation: An us-vs-them applause line aimed at the opposition rather than persuading the unconvinced.

charisma.statement: I reject the characterisation that the member has made, and that's for this reason: I would agree that each of the individuals who served on the Health New Zealand board are capable individuals, and I believe that every one of them was on that board because they wanted to do better for New Zealanders in the health system. It is also my view that they were given an almost impossible task by a Government that completely botched an ideological merger of the DHB system.
charisma.explanation: Conciliatory toward the directors but still frames it as a partisan attack on the prior government.

charisma.statement: What is important and what I wish the member would join me in is fixing it.
charisma.explanation: Invites the opposition member to work together on the shared problem.

charisma.statement: What I would say is stakeholder groups, Opposition parties, Governments, and Māori have all called for Oranga Tamariki to change. This is what change looks like. It's not an option to keep the status quo. To do so would be to say we're happy with how the organisation is running now and delivering for children, and we know it's not. So I would urge the Opposition to get on board and make sure that we can enable change that's going to be enduring.
charisma.explanation: Appeals for cross-party buy-in but pairs it with a false-dichotomy 'change vs happy with status quo' framing.

charisma.statement: Heaps of value. This fund will help promote regional events that will deliver a high return on investment and encourage visitors to explore beyond the main centres. There is life in New Zealand outside the big cities.
charisma.explanation: Warm regional booster tone but not aimed at persuading opponents.

charisma.statement: As I've clarified, there is no counting in different ways. We have clarified. But what I would say that is important to police morale is that we are getting tough on crime, and we are making police able to do their job... We are not the Government that will be soft on gangs. We will support the morale of the police and allow them to get back to catching the bad guys.
charisma.explanation: 'Soft on gangs' / 'catching the bad guys' is a partisan rallying framing, not consensus-building.

charisma.statement: The Independent Police Conduct Authority takes such a significant role in ensuring that we have significant checks and balances on the conduct of our police. This is more important than ever, particularly when we see legislation that has come through this House that increases the powers of police and makes some of their work far more dangerous at times.
charisma.explanation: Constructive, institution-focused tone building support for the oversight body.

charisma.statement: I stand with absolute pride that National-led Governments have continued to support the establishment of various kura kaupapa, wānanga, and kōhanga reo throughout the last four decades.
charisma.explanation: Proud, positive framing but responds to a partisan prompt from Peters rather than reaching across.

charisma.statement: in the small town that I grew up in in Tokoroa, it was a common occurrence to have breath checks on our main road every week, and I was pulled over multiple times as a young person... but I've never been pulled up in Wellington. There's a huge difference between the way that some communities, particularly those with low socio-economic indicators and those that are predominantly Māori or Pacific, are more heavily policed than other communities.
charisma.explanation: Personal, relatable storytelling that humanises the argument for oversight.

charisma.statement: Actually having New Zealanders who are prepared to stand up and be appointed to important bodies like this is great, and I want to just acknowledge him.
charisma.explanation: Warm, inclusive tone recognising service across the appointment process.

charisma.statement: I move, That the House sends its condolences to all those who have lost loved ones and livelihoods in Typhoon Gaemi, also known as Typhoon Carina, in the Philippines that struck a range of countries in South East Asia and North Asia from 19 July to 27 July, and notes that the New Zealand Government stands ready to consider and respond to any requests for assistance from affected countries to aid recovery efforts.
charisma.explanation: Seeks unanimous, cross-House expression of sympathy and solidarity.

civility.statement: I am not advised as to how many of them were Labour voters, but I'm guessing some. Let us not forget that members opposite voted against it.
civility.explanation: A political jibe about how opponents voted, but attacks a vote not a person.

civility.statement: I reject the characterisation that the member has made, and that's for this reason: I would agree that each of the individuals who served on the Health New Zealand board are capable individuals, and I believe that every one of them was on that board because they wanted to do better for New Zealanders in the health system. It is also my view that they were given an almost impossible task by a Government that completely botched an ideological merger of the DHB system.
civility.explanation: Defends the board members personally as capable and well-intentioned; keeps criticism aimed at the previous government's policy rather than individuals.

civility.statement: Yes, in the context in which I said it, which was in relation to the proposed Oranga Tamariki organisational restructure. From the beginning, the safety of children has been at the forefront of all decision making about the proposed restructure, and front-line managers and staff who report to them have been out of scope of this process. However, I do recognise that this has been an unsettling time for all staff at Oranga Tamariki, front-line or otherwise, and I just want to take the opportunity to acknowledge this.
civility.explanation: Respectfully acknowledges staff distress rather than dismissing concerns.

civility.statement: Because the patients have also seen the layers and layers of management that that Government put in as part of their botched health reforms, and we're reconnecting the front line.
civility.explanation: Criticises the prior government's policy ('botched reforms') rather than individuals.

civility.statement: We have inherited a system that cares a lot about paying consultants to write business cases and not enough about delivering and looking after the investments that we already have and that we need.
civility.explanation: Pointed criticism of the system/previous approach rather than a personal attack.

civility.statement: There are many. At the expert panel stage of the process, conditions will be set to protect the environment. As the bill is currently drafted, in deciding whether a project is eligible to be referred to a panel, Ministers may consider whether the project will address significant environmental issues. Ministers may decline an application if Ministers consider the project may have significant adverse effects on the environment. Applications will include an assessment of environmental effects, with an assessment against relevant national direction, regional, and district planning documents. The member should read the bill.
civility.explanation: 'The member should read the bill' is a dismissive jab at the questioner.

civility.statement: The Hon Dr Nick Smith is a friend and someone who I have a lot of time and respect for. I haven't seen those full comments and I haven't seen them in their full context, so it's difficult to proffer a view without that.
civility.explanation: Warm, respectful reference to a colleague while declining to comment.

civility.statement: Can the Minister confirm that he is actually able to count to 500, and, if not, is that why he gave the ministerial delegation to Casey Costello?
civility.explanation: Mocks the Minister's basic competence — a personal cheap shot rather than policy critique.

civility.statement: Did his office receive an email from Casey Costello's office that requested, "a copy of the Police briefing on options on different way[s] to count the 500", and does he plan to boost police morale with some creative counting?
civility.explanation: The 'creative counting' sarcasm is a jab, though it attaches to a substantive documented allegation.

civility.statement: The Independent Police Conduct Authority takes such a significant role in ensuring that we have significant checks and balances on the conduct of our police. This is more important than ever, particularly when we see legislation that has come through this House that increases the powers of police and makes some of their work far more dangerous at times.
civility.explanation: Substantive, respectful remarks in support of the appointments and the IPCA's role.

civility.statement: given that the National Party brought in kura kaupapa Māori, why is he now being lectured on it?
civility.explanation: A partisan swipe at the questioner's standing rather than the policy issue.

civility.statement: my colleague Kahurangi Carter made the comment that many New Zealanders would rather walk down a dark alleyway with a patched gang member than with a police officer, and this caused some disagreement from the Minister. But the reality is that this is a statement of fact and that is how some people feel.
civility.explanation: Provocative toward police as an institution but framed as reporting community feeling, not a personal attack.

civility.statement: With respect to the report that has been delivered today, Question of privilege concerning the conduct of a member during the committee of the whole House, I apologise unreservedly for my conduct in the House on the evening of 1 May 2024.
civility.explanation: An unqualified apology accepting responsibility for her own conduct.

civility.statement: I wish to apologise to Tanya Unkovich for comments I made at a meeting of the Health Committee on Wednesday, 19 June 2024.
civility.explanation: A direct, personal apology for earlier comments.

civility.statement: Actually having New Zealanders who are prepared to stand up and be appointed to important bodies like this is great, and I want to just acknowledge him.
civility.explanation: Gracious acknowledgement of an outgoing member's public service.

civility.statement: I move, That the House sends its condolences to all those who have lost loved ones and livelihoods in Typhoon Gaemi, also known as Typhoon Carina, in the Philippines that struck a range of countries in South East Asia and North Asia from 19 July to 27 July, and notes that the New Zealand Government stands ready to consider and respond to any requests for assistance from affected countries to aid recovery efforts.
civility.explanation: A non-partisan motion of condolence and offer of assistance.

authenticity.statement: Yes, in the context in which I said it, which was in relation to the proposed Oranga Tamariki organisational restructure. From the beginning, the safety of children has been at the forefront of all decision making about the proposed restructure, and front-line managers and staff who report to them have been out of scope of this process. However, I do recognise that this has been an unsettling time for all staff at Oranga Tamariki, front-line or otherwise, and I just want to take the opportunity to acknowledge this.
authenticity.explanation: Defends a 'no impact on frontline services' guarantee by restricting its scope, which sits in tension with reported community-provider funding cuts.

authenticity.statement: I stand with absolute pride that National-led Governments have continued to support the establishment of various kura kaupapa, wānanga, and kōhanga reo throughout the last four decades.
authenticity.explanation: Claims a consistent National record on Māori education; a defensible positioning but asserted rather than evidenced in the text.

authenticity.statement: With respect to the report that has been delivered today, Question of privilege concerning the conduct of a member during the committee of the whole House, I apologise unreservedly for my conduct in the House on the evening of 1 May 2024.
authenticity.explanation: Words align with accepting the privileges finding; a consistent acknowledgement of her actions.

authenticity.statement: I wish to apologise to Tanya Unkovich for comments I made at a meeting of the Health Committee on Wednesday, 19 June 2024.
authenticity.explanation: Takes ownership of her own prior conduct, aligning words with accountability.

specificity.statement: From tomorrow, 3.5 million individuals will keep more of what they earn. We are adjusting tax brackets and eligibility for the independent earner tax credit after years of inflation dragging Kiwis into higher and higher tax brackets. We're boosting Working for Families payments by up to $50 a fortnight
specificity.explanation: Names figures (3.5m people, up to $50/fortnight), a date ('from tomorrow'), and named mechanisms (tax brackets, IETC, Working for Families).

specificity.statement: Yes, we're going to work incredibly hard to lower child poverty across the country.
specificity.explanation: Vague aspiration ('work incredibly hard') with no target, figure, or timeframe.

specificity.statement: We are determined to rebuild this economy so that we can grow the prosperity and wealth of all families and take children out of poverty.
specificity.explanation: Platitude with no mechanism or measure.

specificity.statement: Ninety-four percent of households across New Zealand are going to get tax relief; 83 percent of individuals in this country are going to get tax relief.
specificity.explanation: Cites concrete percentages but not the amounts each group receives.

specificity.statement: Why, then, did his Government quietly weaken child poverty targets last month, allowing approximately 23,000 more children to be pushed into hardship?
specificity.explanation: Precise claim with a figure (≈23,000 children) and timeframe ('last month').

specificity.statement: How is it fair that his tax cut package, which he keeps saying will benefit low and middle income earners—while analysis in fact shows that 64 percent of the benefit goes to the top 40 percent of households—will see children and families struggling the most get nothing because they're on benefits?
specificity.explanation: Cites a concrete distributional statistic (64% to top 40% of households).

specificity.statement: Who was that laser focus concentrated on: pensioners, who can expect to get just $2.50 a week; minimum wage earners, who can expect to get $12.50; or one Philip Morris, who just got $216 million in tax cuts?
specificity.explanation: Concrete contrasting figures ($2.50, $12.50, $216 million) naming specific beneficiaries.

specificity.statement: There's been far too much handwringing. There's been far too much culture wars afflicting economic development. These will be opportunities where we can elevate the importance of mining. We can lead a national discussion about the role of rare-earth minerals, including vanadium located in the iron sands off the coast of Taranaki.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete themes (mining, rare-earth minerals, vanadium in Taranaki iron sands) though the summits' outputs remain undefined.

specificity.statement: There's no place in these serious debates for Green quackery. This will focus on those measurable types of investments... which is to boost resilience through ensuring that our river systems and our catchments are better managed with flood management.
specificity.explanation: Gestures at 'measurable' investments and flood/catchment management but without figures or named projects.

specificity.statement: It's important that we respond with alacrity and work with partners in the regions so that we adapt to cope with the inevitable changes in our quality of life, in our infrastructure, as weather worsens.
specificity.explanation: Vague on the actual projects, no names or figures.

specificity.statement: Income tax thresholds are being increased tomorrow. The in-work tax credit for low and middle income working families is being increased tomorrow. The independent earner tax credit is being extended to $70,000 of income tomorrow.
specificity.explanation: Three concrete, dated policy changes including the $70,000 IETC threshold.

specificity.statement: There is no doubt that the Government is not borrowing for tax relief in this Budget... Every single dollar of that is funded from baseline savings: closing stupid Labour programmes like industry transformation plans; a climate dividend; commercial buildings depreciation; taxing online casino operators... revenue from immigration levies; replacing first-year fees free with final-year fees free; and investment in tax compliance activities.
specificity.explanation: Itemises the specific savings and revenue lines said to fund the $3.68bn package.

specificity.statement: No, and I refer the member to the Treasury's analysis in the Budget update, which says... 'The decisions taken through Budget 2024 will on balance reduce the contribution fiscal policy is making to inflation pressure. Tax policy changes will boost aggregate demand, but this is more than offset by lower government spending and lower allowances compared to the Half Year Update.'
specificity.explanation: Precise sourced quotation on fiscal-inflation impact.

specificity.statement: How can she say the Government is not borrowing extra for tax cuts when her own Budget shows that the income tax cuts cost $10 billion and the Government is issuing an additional $12 billion of debt bonds?
specificity.explanation: Concrete figures ($10bn tax cost, $12bn additional bonds) sharpen the challenge.

specificity.statement: NZTA conducted a review of temporary traffic management at 800 maintenance work sites on the State highway network across the country in February and found that 145 of these sites were not needed... Auckland Council Mayor Wayne Brown has also released a report showing that $145 million of expenditure has been incurred by his council group every single year.
specificity.explanation: Precise figures (800 sites, 145 unnecessary, $145m/year) and a named source.

specificity.statement: When I became transport Minister, I asked NZTA to outline how much money has been spent by NZTA each year for the past three years on temporary traffic management, and was advised this information was not available as it was not compiled. This is unacceptable. That's why the Government will be requiring NZTA and all road-controlling authorities to report quarterly on the amount of taxpayers' money they are spending.
specificity.explanation: Names the concrete mechanism (quarterly reporting by NZTA and all road-controlling authorities).

specificity.statement: By passing this bill, our Government is restoring the right of local communities to determine whether to introduce Māori wards... reinstating binding polls for Māori wards and constituencies, a policy that was put in place by the Helen Clark Government.
specificity.explanation: Concrete mechanisms and a deadline (rescind/poll by 6 September, 2025 election timing).

specificity.statement: First of all, this Government does not have boot camps. The Government has begun a military-style academy pilot... The ten young people... each young person on the pilot has received from a clinical psychologist. Other lessons included the need to focus on the transition from the residential environment back into the community... each young person will have a mentor... for the three-month in-residence and nine-month community phase.
specificity.explanation: Concrete details: 10 participants, clinical-psychologist assessments, mentors, 3-month residential + 9-month community structure.

specificity.statement: I've seen evidence that the previous approaches to youth crime saw a 291 percent increase in ram raids over the last six years. In 2023, over 85 percent of offenders were younger than 18.
specificity.explanation: Precise statistics (291% increase over six years, 85% of offenders under 18 in 2023).

specificity.statement: I recently announced the Government will change the Sentencing Act to ensure real consequences for crime. This will cap the use of sentencing discounts at 40 percent, introduce a new aggravating factor to address serious retail crime, encourage the use of cumulative sentences, and a raft of other changes.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete measures including the 40% sentencing-discount cap and new aggravating factor.

specificity.statement: In response to a significant increase in retail crime over the past five years, with the total number of reported victimisations up 86 percent, the Government tasked its ministerial advisory group... with developing specific proposals to address urgent challenges in retail crime.
specificity.explanation: Cites a concrete statistic (victimisations up 86% over five years) and a named mechanism.

specificity.statement: Gangs have, for some time, been allowed to behave as if they're above the law; they are not. [The Bill] prohibits the display of gang insignia in public places, gives police the ability to issue dispersal notices... creates new non-consorting orders, and amends the Sentencing Act to make gang membership, on its own, an aggravating factor.
specificity.explanation: Enumerates the concrete provisions of the Gangs Legislation Amendment Bill.

specificity.statement: The Tertiary Education Commission has recently exercised its statutory intervention power to require Te Pūkenga to obtain specialist external help to conduct the necessary cost-out work... The ITP sector faces significant financial sustainability issues that were not addressed by Te Pūkenga. This work should have gone ahead four years ago.
specificity.explanation: Names the statutory mechanism and the cost-out and ITP-network re-establishment tasks.

specificity.statement: from tomorrow, 31 July, 11 pages of overly prescriptive affordability regulations will no longer be part of the Credit Contracts and Consumer Finance Act... There are still stiff penalties for people who do not comply under the CCCFA—including $200,000 for individuals, or up to $600,000 for other entities.
specificity.explanation: Precise date, scope (11 pages), and penalty figures ($200,000 / $600,000).

specificity.statement: The regulations treated borrowers like children. Borrowers were required to explain why they did things like buy an occasional coffee, join a gym, or treated the family to fish and chips every now and again—even when they clearly could afford to.
specificity.explanation: Concrete examples of the checks, though impressionistic rather than quantified.

specificity.statement: A few days ago, Federated Farmers released their 31st farm confidence survey. Overall, it showed a weakening of farmer confidence with a net 66 percent of farmers pointing out that current economic conditions are very challenging and that profit margins for many are squeezed.
specificity.explanation: Cites the specific survey (31st) and a net figure (66%).

veracity.statement: From tomorrow, 3.5 million individuals will keep more of what they earn. We are adjusting tax brackets and eligibility for the independent earner tax credit after years of inflation dragging Kiwis into higher and higher tax brackets. We're boosting Working for Families payments by up to $50 a fortnight
veracity.explanation: The tax package and WFF changes did take effect on 31 July 2024; broadly accurate, though '3.5 million' and framing of benefit are favourable.

veracity.statement: Ninety-four percent of households across New Zealand are going to get tax relief; 83 percent of individuals in this country are going to get tax relief.
veracity.explanation: Coverage figures are plausibly accurate but omit the distributional context that changes the meaning of 'benefit low and middle income earners'.

veracity.statement: Well, the great news is that we are a Government that is introducing tax relief for the first time in 14 years. We are lifting the tax thresholds so that people don't get caught in higher tax brackets they don't need to be in.
veracity.explanation: 'First tax relief in 14 years' is a defensible claim about threshold indexation, though rhetorically framed.

veracity.statement: There's no evidence of that. But what I would say is... They assumed that people would get a prescription every single week, but there's actually a $100 cap on those fees per household.
veracity.explanation: The $100 prescription cap per household is a real policy feature; accurate factual correction.

veracity.statement: Who was that laser focus concentrated on: pensioners, who can expect to get just $2.50 a week; minimum wage earners, who can expect to get $12.50; or one Philip Morris, who just got $216 million in tax cuts?
veracity.explanation: The pensioner/minimum-wage figures and the tobacco-tax/'Philip Morris' framing are rhetorically selective; directionally grounded but the $216m attribution to one firm is contestable.

veracity.statement: There is no doubt that the Government is not borrowing for tax relief in this Budget... Every single dollar of that is funded from baseline savings: closing stupid Labour programmes like industry transformation plans; a climate dividend; commercial buildings depreciation; taxing online casino operators... revenue from immigration levies; replacing first-year fees free with final-year fees free; and investment in tax compliance activities.
veracity.explanation: The funding items are real, but whether they fully offset the package (vs simultaneous bond issuance) is genuinely contested, as the questioner notes.

veracity.statement: NZTA conducted a review of temporary traffic management at 800 maintenance work sites on the State highway network across the country in February and found that 145 of these sites were not needed... Auckland Council Mayor Wayne Brown has also released a report showing that $145 million of expenditure has been incurred by his council group every single year.
veracity.explanation: Attributes concrete figures to an NZTA review and an Auckland Council report; plausible and sourced, though selected to support the case.

veracity.statement: I've seen evidence that the previous approaches to youth crime saw a 291 percent increase in ram raids over the last six years. In 2023, over 85 percent of offenders were younger than 18.
veracity.explanation: Cites concrete figures but attributes a 'ram raid' surge to 'previous approaches' as causation; the numbers themselves are plausible if selectively framed.

veracity.statement: In response to a significant increase in retail crime over the past five years, with the total number of reported victimisations up 86 percent, the Government tasked its ministerial advisory group... with developing specific proposals to address urgent challenges in retail crime.
veracity.explanation: The 86% figure is presented as an official statistic; plausible but unsourced in the exchange.

veracity.statement: A few days ago, Federated Farmers released their 31st farm confidence survey. Overall, it showed a weakening of farmer confidence with a net 66 percent of farmers pointing out that current economic conditions are very challenging and that profit margins for many are squeezed.
veracity.explanation: Attributes concrete figures to a named, identifiable Federated Farmers survey; verifiable and plausibly accurate.

strength.statement: From tomorrow, 3.5 million individuals will keep more of what they earn. We are adjusting tax brackets and eligibility for the independent earner tax credit after years of inflation dragging Kiwis into higher and higher tax brackets. We're boosting Working for Families payments by up to $50 a fortnight
strength.explanation: A concrete commitment that was actually enacted the following day, with the Government responsible for delivery.

strength.statement: Income tax thresholds are being increased tomorrow. The in-work tax credit for low and middle income working families is being increased tomorrow. The independent earner tax credit is being extended to $70,000 of income tomorrow.
strength.explanation: Concrete measures taking effect the next day, delivered by the Government.

strength.statement: When I became transport Minister, I asked NZTA to outline how much money has been spent by NZTA each year for the past three years on temporary traffic management, and was advised this information was not available as it was not compiled. This is unacceptable. That's why the Government will be requiring NZTA and all road-controlling authorities to report quarterly on the amount of taxpayers' money they are spending.
strength.explanation: A stated commitment to a new reporting regime; announced/underway rather than yet demonstrably delivered.

strength.statement: By passing this bill, our Government is restoring the right of local communities to determine whether to introduce Māori wards... reinstating binding polls for Māori wards and constituencies, a policy that was put in place by the Helen Clark Government.
strength.explanation: A coalition commitment being enacted at third reading — delivery of a stated policy.

strength.statement: First of all, this Government does not have boot camps. The Government has begun a military-style academy pilot... The ten young people... each young person on the pilot has received from a clinical psychologist. Other lessons included the need to focus on the transition from the residential environment back into the community... each young person will have a mentor... for the three-month in-residence and nine-month community phase.
strength.explanation: A committed policy actually launched ('got under way yesterday'), though outcomes are unproven.

strength.statement: I recently announced the Government will change the Sentencing Act to ensure real consequences for crime. This will cap the use of sentencing discounts at 40 percent, introduce a new aggravating factor to address serious retail crime, encourage the use of cumulative sentences, and a raft of other changes.
strength.explanation: Announced legislative changes in progress rather than yet enacted; commitment with delivery pending.

strength.statement: Gangs have, for some time, been allowed to behave as if they're above the law; they are not. [The Bill] prohibits the display of gang insignia in public places, gives police the ability to issue dispersal notices... creates new non-consorting orders, and amends the Sentencing Act to make gang membership, on its own, an aggravating factor.
strength.explanation: A bill at second reading — committed and advancing, delivery not yet complete.

strength.statement: from tomorrow, 31 July, 11 pages of overly prescriptive affordability regulations will no longer be part of the Credit Contracts and Consumer Finance Act... There are still stiff penalties for people who do not comply under the CCCFA—including $200,000 for individuals, or up to $600,000 for other entities.
strength.explanation: A concrete regulatory change taking effect the next day — delivered.

forthrightness.statement: Yes, we're going to work incredibly hard to lower child poverty across the country.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked specifically whether he stands by the 2023 debate commitment to halve child poverty by 2028; he affirms effort but never confirms the specific target or timeframe.

forthrightness.statement: We are determined to rebuild this economy so that we can grow the prosperity and wealth of all families and take children out of poverty.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked why his Government weakened child poverty targets, allowing ~23,000 more children into hardship; he pivots entirely to a generic economic-rebuild line and never addresses the target change.

forthrightness.statement: Ninety-four percent of households across New Zealand are going to get tax relief; 83 percent of individuals in this country are going to get tax relief.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked about distribution (64% of benefit to top 40% of households, beneficiaries getting nothing); he answers with headline coverage figures and never engages the distributional or benefit-recipient point.

forthrightness.statement: No, we're not saying that, but we are lifting tax thresholds so that families get to keep more of what they earn and support their own children.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly rejects the loaded premise ('do children deserve poverty') but then redirects to tax thresholds rather than the beneficiary-family situation raised.

forthrightness.statement: I have read the report, and that's why this Government is working incredibly hard to rebuild the economy, to kill inflation, and to lower the cost of living, so that, actually, we can make this country more prosperous.
forthrightness.explanation: Confirms he read the report but dodges the actual question — why he is choosing to allow more children into poverty — by reverting to economic talking points.

forthrightness.statement: Well, the great news is that we are a Government that is introducing tax relief for the first time in 14 years. We are lifting the tax thresholds so that people don't get caught in higher tax brackets they don't need to be in.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether hiking car registration fees and expanding road-user charges raised or lowered the cost of living; he answers about tax cuts instead, which the questioner's point of order explicitly flags as non-responsive.

forthrightness.statement: Yeah, and what I'd say is that a majority of New Zealanders don't use public transport, and some of them actually drive... But what they all certainly appreciate is tax relief for low and middle income workers, a group of people who the Labour Party used to care about, but it has lost its way. David Parker cares about them, but the Labour Party doesn't.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether charging children more for public transport increased family costs; he sidesteps to fuel/ute tax and an attack on Labour without addressing the transport-fare point.

forthrightness.statement: There's no evidence of that. But what I would say is... They assumed that people would get a prescription every single week, but there's actually a $100 cap on those fees per household.
forthrightness.explanation: Denies the causal claim about prescription co-payments and hospitals, then partly answers by disputing Labour's costing rather than the health-outcome premise.

forthrightness.statement: I'd just say to the member: are you against low and middle income working New Zealanders getting tax relief?
forthrightness.explanation: Asked who the tax cuts benefit (pensioners $2.50, minimum wage $12.50, or Philip Morris $216m); he answers a question with a question and does not respond at all.

forthrightness.statement: It's important that we respond with alacrity and work with partners in the regions so that we adapt to cope with the inevitable changes in our quality of life, in our infrastructure, as weather worsens.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked for examples of projects supported through the Regional Infrastructure Fund; gives a general aspiration about adapting to weather rather than naming projects.

forthrightness.statement: There is no doubt that the Government is not borrowing for tax relief in this Budget... Every single dollar of that is funded from baseline savings: closing stupid Labour programmes like industry transformation plans; a climate dividend; commercial buildings depreciation; taxing online casino operators... revenue from immigration levies; replacing first-year fees free with final-year fees free; and investment in tax compliance activities.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly answers the borrowing question with a detailed funding breakdown.

forthrightness.statement: No, and I refer the member to the Treasury's analysis in the Budget update, which says... 'The decisions taken through Budget 2024 will on balance reduce the contribution fiscal policy is making to inflation pressure. Tax policy changes will boost aggregate demand, but this is more than offset by lower government spending and lower allowances compared to the Half Year Update.'
forthrightness.explanation: Directly rejects the premise and supplies the evidence relied upon.

forthrightness.statement: Well, I often agree with the leader of the ACT Party, who I've found to make incisive and cogent remarks about public policy. And if members opposite, when they were in Government, had listened to the leader of the ACT Party... we wouldn't be in the fiscal mess that we are in right now.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether she has 'given up on New Zealanders' given higher peak net debt; deflects into praise of the ACT leader and blame of the previous Government.

forthrightness.statement: Oh well, I've always found Chris Bishop to be a very incisive and cogent commentator on the Crown books, and I often take his advice and I will continue to do so.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to reconcile calling $104bn debt a 'blowout' with $114bn under his own watch; dodges entirely with a self-referential joke.

forthrightness.statement: When I became transport Minister, I asked NZTA to outline how much money has been spent by NZTA each year for the past three years on temporary traffic management, and was advised this information was not available as it was not compiled. This is unacceptable. That's why the Government will be requiring NZTA and all road-controlling authorities to report quarterly on the amount of taxpayers' money they are spending.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly answers why the reporting requirement is being introduced, with the specific rationale.

forthrightness.statement: First of all, this Government does not have boot camps. The Government has begun a military-style academy pilot... The ten young people... each young person on the pilot has received from a clinical psychologist. Other lessons included the need to focus on the transition from the residential environment back into the community... each young person will have a mentor... for the three-month in-residence and nine-month community phase.
forthrightness.explanation: Substantively addresses the design and evidence basis of the pilot.

forthrightness.statement: Yes, I do agree that boot camps in the past were horrific and did cause harm to people who went on those boot camps. They were run inappropriately, with staff who were not trained, in a remote isolated area with no way to actually seek help.
forthrightness.explanation: Concedes directly that past boot camps caused harm rather than deflecting.

forthrightness.statement: Nobody can guarantee the actions of others, but what we can do is make sure we put everything in place to make sure that the risks are as low as possible and that, if something does happen, we act quickly and efficiently and in the right way.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to guarantee no abuse; honestly declines to guarantee and explains the mitigation approach rather than dodging.

forthrightness.statement: These young people are in a youth justice facility currently because they have committed serious offences. It is obvious that approaches that have been tried beforehand haven't worked. That is why we are trying a new approach.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked what alternative interventions were considered and why dismissed; she asserts past approaches failed but does not name the alternatives or the advice, as the point of order flags.

forthrightness.statement: Well, I always agree with the Prime Minister. And, of course, we're not setting up a working group to wait for two years. I've made it very clear that I want that group, which will be chaired by Sunny Kaushal, to come up with specific proposals, quickly.
forthrightness.explanation: Addresses the apparent contradiction (Luxon's 'no working groups' line vs a two-year group) by disputing the two-year characterisation and naming the chair.

forthrightness.statement: Yes, I stand by that statement in the context that it was given back in December 2023.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly affirms she stands by the earlier statement, with a caveat about context/timing.

forthrightness.statement: The Tertiary Education Commission has recently exercised its statutory intervention power to require Te Pūkenga to obtain specialist external help to conduct the necessary cost-out work... The ITP sector faces significant financial sustainability issues that were not addressed by Te Pūkenga. This work should have gone ahead four years ago.
forthrightness.explanation: Explains why consultants were engaged (TEC statutory intervention), addressing the question, while shifting blame to the sector's history.

forthrightness.statement: I don't recall being given that advice from Te Pūkenga—they may have given advice to the TEC, who they report to.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether Te Pūkenga advised her that ceasing restructuring would add $53m in costs; answers with non-recollection and deflection to TEC rather than confirming or denying.

forthrightness.statement: This Government is undertaking considerable work to take cost out of Te Pūkenga. We have asked for the head office to be reduced, we are looking at the funding decreases that were brought in by the previous Government... There is a range of work going on to take out the millions of dollars that have been wasted by Te Pūkenga.
forthrightness.explanation: Pressed on how she could forget $53m in advised costs; pivots entirely to generic cost-out activity and blame of the previous Government without addressing the specific correspondence.

forthrightness.statement: Yes, I agree with the Prime Minister, particularly when he said, "it's actually been a botched restructuring and a botched merger that actually hasn't delivered an efficient operating model."... That's why this Government has taken decisive action by appointing a commissioner to turn around Health New Zealand.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly agrees with the PM's characterisation and states the action taken (commissioner appointment).

forthrightness.statement: We collaborated with Health New Zealand and we produced the table that was then published in public domain, which we stand by.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether he or his office created or changed the '14 layers' list; answers that it was produced collaboratively and published, but does not squarely address whether the list was changed.

civility.statement: Oh, the ventriloquist is away today, that's right! Oh, there we go!
civility.explanation: A personal jibe implying the opposition leader is a mouthpiece, contributing nothing to substance.

civility.statement: Yeah, and what I'd say is that a majority of New Zealanders don't use public transport, and some of them actually drive... But what they all certainly appreciate is tax relief for low and middle income workers, a group of people who the Labour Party used to care about, but it has lost its way. David Parker cares about them, but the Labour Party doesn't.
civility.explanation: Personal/political attack ('Labour has lost its way'; singling out David Parker against his party) rather than engaging the substance.

civility.statement: Why, then, did his Government quietly weaken child poverty targets last month, allowing approximately 23,000 more children to be pushed into hardship?
civility.explanation: Pointed and accusatory ('quietly weaken') but directed at a policy decision rather than personal character.

civility.statement: Is he saying that children deserve to live in poverty if their parents' income comes from benefits?
civility.explanation: Aggressive framing that attributes an unstated view, though aimed at policy consequences rather than personal insult.

civility.statement: Climate change—say climate change.
civility.explanation: A heckling interjection challenging the minister to name climate change; provocative but issue-focused.

civility.statement: Who was that laser focus concentrated on: pensioners, who can expect to get just $2.50 a week; minimum wage earners, who can expect to get $12.50; or one Philip Morris, who just got $216 million in tax cuts?
civility.explanation: Sharp juxtaposition to embarrass the Government, but targets policy outcomes and a corporate beneficiary, not a personal attack.

civility.statement: He couldn't find any notes in his folder there for that one, Mr Speaker.
civility.explanation: A mocking jab at the PM's preparedness rather than a substantive point.

civility.statement: There's been far too much handwringing. There's been far too much culture wars afflicting economic development. These will be opportunities where we can elevate the importance of mining. We can lead a national discussion about the role of rare-earth minerals, including vanadium located in the iron sands off the coast of Taranaki.
civility.explanation: Dismissive framing ('handwringing', 'culture wars') but aimed at approaches rather than persons.

civility.statement: I don't want any more Green ideological sludge from that side of the House. This is a pure economic development approach. Co-governance is gone; co-investment is in.
civility.explanation: Derisive labelling ('Green ideological sludge') of an opponent's contribution — dismissive, non-substantive.

civility.statement: There's no place in these serious debates for Green quackery. This will focus on those measurable types of investments... which is to boost resilience through ensuring that our river systems and our catchments are better managed with flood management.
civility.explanation: 'Green quackery' is a dismissive personal-adjacent slur on opponents, though paired with a policy point on flood management.

civility.statement: Well, I often agree with the leader of the ACT Party, who I've found to make incisive and cogent remarks about public policy. And if members opposite, when they were in Government, had listened to the leader of the ACT Party... we wouldn't be in the fiscal mess that we are in right now.
civility.explanation: Partisan but engages the fiscal argument rather than personal insult.

civility.statement: Oh well, I've always found Chris Bishop to be a very incisive and cogent commentator on the Crown books, and I often take his advice and I will continue to do so.
civility.explanation: Light, self-deprecating humour rather than an attack, though it evades the substance.

civility.statement: They rammed it through to get rid of democracy because that's what that side of the House does. They don't believe in democracy, and we do.
civility.explanation: Sweeping personal-motive attack asserting opponents 'don't believe in democracy'.

civility.statement: The people of New Zealand rejected your form of democracy, Willie Jackson. They rejected it on 14 October, and they voted in the coalition Government to restore local democracy in New Zealand.
civility.explanation: Directly personalised at a named member; combative though tied to the election result.

civility.statement: You're not in Mexico now. We don't do things like that here.
civility.explanation: An interjection taken as a xenophobic personal barb at a member, which he was required to withdraw and apologise for.

civility.statement: Yes, I agree with the Prime Minister, particularly when he said, "it's actually been a botched restructuring and a botched merger that actually hasn't delivered an efficient operating model."... That's why this Government has taken decisive action by appointing a commissioner to turn around Health New Zealand.
civility.explanation: 'Botched' is harsh but aimed at the restructuring, not persons.

civility.statement: Does his private health insurance cover injuries sustained while being thrown under the bus by the PM?
civility.explanation: A witty but personal jibe implying the Minister was scapegoated; more mockery than substance.

civility.statement: Can the Minister confirm that some of the people browsing on the Treasury's tax calculator have been found, by analysis, to be Labour voters from Wadestown browsing in incognito mode?
civility.explanation: A partisan joke at Labour voters' expense; light-hearted but a jab rather than substance.

charisma.statement: Yeah, and what I'd say is that a majority of New Zealanders don't use public transport, and some of them actually drive... But what they all certainly appreciate is tax relief for low and middle income workers, a group of people who the Labour Party used to care about, but it has lost its way. David Parker cares about them, but the Labour Party doesn't.
charisma.explanation: Rallies his own side by dividing the opposition rather than seeking common ground.

charisma.statement: I don't want any more Green ideological sludge from that side of the House. This is a pure economic development approach. Co-governance is gone; co-investment is in.
