authenticity.statement: We came in and we told our people we are not the moderate, we are not the incremental party; we are the transformational party, because our people are hurting so much and so are our communities.

authenticity.explanation: Frames her support for the rules as consistent with a commitment she personally made; words align with her stated position on process.

authenticity.statement: we will not be silenced, we will not be assimilated, we will not be subjugated, and we make no apology for being absolutely unapologetically, unfettered, unbridled Māori human beings.
authenticity.explanation: Consistent with Te Pāti Māori's stated refusal to apologise and their conduct in this debate; the defiant stance matches their actions.

charisma.explanation: Blanket us-vs-them framing that demonises the Government wholesale and makes no attempt to persuade the other side.

charisma.statement: We want to teach our next generation that you can sit around a table, you can have a debate, and you can disagree, and walk away, agreeing to disagree, without slinging insults at each other and without using bullying tactics to try and get our own way.

charisma.statement: I am astounded by the last three ACT Party speakers, who seemed far more offended about alleged finger guns than actual gun violence, children living in poverty, or workers being exploited.
charisma.explanation: Rallies his own side by mocking opponents; makes no attempt to persuade them.

charisma.explanation: Directly addresses opponents on assumed shared values, inviting them to common ground rather than attacking.

charisma.statement: Make no mistake: this Government’s agenda is a war on many. It is a war on Māori. It is a war on wāhine, who refuse to be silent. It is a war to takatāpui, who will not shrink. It is a war on many families living in poverty

charisma.statement: I acknowledge members across the House for their words, for their passion, and for their commitment to their issues.

charisma.explanation: Frames rules as the shared protection that allows everyone's voice, an inclusive appeal.

strength.statement: Since the Active Investor Plus visa opened on 1 April, we've received 189 applications. strength.explanation: Credits a delivered policy change with a measurable jump in applications.

strength.statement: this morning, the Government announced the largest ever funding boost for general practice in our country's history. GPs will receive up to 13.89 percent funding uplift, bringing the total Government funding increase to $175 million for this financial year. That's more than double the highest annual increase there has been since capitation was first rolled out.
strength.explanation: An announced funding commitment — concrete, though delivery/outcomes are still ahead.

specificity.explanation: Names the specific aircraft, the timing (Sunday), and the purpose.

specificity.statement: It's not if but when, and when is when we know we'll have the authority legitimately capable of making the claim that they are the representatives of the people.

specificity.statement: These are not defensive actions under imminent threat, they are not sanctioned by the United Nations Security Council, they are not supported by the international community, and, most crucially, they are not legal under international law.

specificity.statement: We should not accept one set of rules for the powerful and another set of rules for everybody else. We must choose principle, we should choose peace, and we should choose the path of international law.
specificity.explanation: Principled framing with no concrete mechanism or action.

specificity.statement: The Green Party condemns the United States' unlawful and aggressive strikes on Iran, and we call on the Government to do the same.
specificity.explanation: Clear ask (condemnation) but a general position rather than a detailed measure.

rigor.explanation: Presses a consistency argument, though it presumes the 'selective condemnation' premise.

rigor.statement: Dairy products have increased in price because the global dairy price has improved—something that is good for New Zealand's farmers.
rigor.explanation: Sound causal point, but used to sidestep the domestic cost-of-living thrust of the question.

rigor.statement: Governments who, in the midst of global challenges, decide to double, triple, and quadruple down on their operating allowances and send cost of living payments to dead people and French backpackers are making inflation worse, not better.
rigor.explanation: Blends a legitimate fiscal-discipline point with anecdote-driven ridicule.

rigor.statement: Natural gas will play a vital role in energy stability as a low-emission alternative to the coal that was imported by that member's party in the last Government. Until viable, cost-effective, renewable options are in place, we intend to honour our climate change and environmental obligations under this trade agreement.
rigor.explanation: Coherent transition argument, partly leaning on contrast with opponents.

rigor.statement: this is not a subsidy, and I refer the member to the definition of fossil fuel subsidies in the ACCTS agreement. Article 4.3 of the agreement shows a number of flexibilities to enable New Zealand to address risks to energy security and affordability.
rigor.explanation: Grounds the rebuttal in the agreement's own definition and a cited article.

rigor.statement: It does feel like the Green Party have used taxpayer money to commission a report to get on TV, from a lawyer that probably is not involved in this agreement.
rigor.explanation: Ad hominem on the report's authors instead of rebutting its content.

rigor.statement: Is it correct that Budget 2025 appropriates $200 million in contingency for the Crown to take commercial stakes of around 10 to 15 percent in new gasfield developments and commercial exploration, in which the Crown takes a stake and, therefore, receives upside profits, cannot be a subsidy?
rigor.explanation: Argues from the equity-stake structure that an investment yielding profit is not a subsidy — a logical distinction.

civility.statement: ours is a foreign policy of collecting all the facts, hearing all the perspectives, and applying a careful, reasonable, cool-headed approach to the situation—not kneejerk reaction and simplistic moral posturing.
civility.explanation: Frames opponents as engaging in 'kneejerk reaction and simplistic moral posturing' — a disparaging characterisation.

civility.statement: Those in this House who rush to condemn, or call out, one actor or other, or who demand that the Government do the same, should pause to reflect on whether they are seeking to understand and influence what is going on, or simply virtue-signalling about it.
civility.explanation: Characterises opponents' positions as 'virtue-signalling', impugning motive rather than engaging substance.

civility.statement: when it comes to the proxies for Iran that have committed so much terrorism and the loss of thousands of lives—Hamas, Hezbollah, the Houthis, with respect to Iran—the Greens have been not a syllable, not a sound, not a mutter, not a murmur, no condemnation whatsoever. On October the 7th, that outrageous terrorism of 1,200 people and 200 people kidnapped or abducted, there was not a word
civility.explanation: Attacks the Greens' character/motives ('not a syllable') rather than engaging their argument.

civility.statement: I know all your track record; it takes five seconds to examine it.
civility.explanation: A dismissive personal jab at an interjecting member rather than substantive engagement.

civility.statement: in August 2021, the then Prime Minister and the Labour Government, supported by the Greens, entered the discussions on AUKUS Pillar II—not a mutter, not a murmur from anybody over here—all the way until the 2023 election.
civility.explanation: Points out opponents' alleged inconsistency but stays largely on the record rather than personal insult.

civility.statement: With the greatest respect, that question just shades into an insult. After all the seriousness that we and Foreign Affairs, working 24/7, have given to this issue over many months and many years, that question is simply a disgraceful insult.
civility.explanation: Dismisses the question as a 'disgraceful insult' rather than engaging it.

civility.statement: we know from the continued genocide in Gaza that a ceasefire with Israel isn't worth the paper it's written on; they have continued to breach and breach and breach ongoing calls and so-called settlements of a ceasefire.
civility.explanation: Harsh but aimed at a state's conduct, not a personal attack on a member.

civility.statement: How is New Zealand contributing to de-escalation and to diplomacy if we continue to only selectively condemn breaches of international law from those countries we think we agree with?
civility.explanation: Pointed but engages the policy of selective condemnation rather than attacking the person.

civility.statement: In the face of a genocide, Winston.
civility.explanation: An interjection using the Minister's first name to rebuke, asserting a contested 'genocide' framing as a jab rather than argument.

civility.statement: The member has drawn some conclusions that I don't necessarily share with him. And if the member had some time between attending to his various responsibilities up and down the motu, including Te Waipounamu, he will see that there are differences in terms of the coalition arrangements in relation to those bills.
civility.explanation: Mildly barbed aside about the member's travels, but largely policy-framed.

civility.statement: Well, if that was true, then it wouldn't, but it's absolutely untrue. Unfortunately, we have an Opposition that lives in a post-fact environment.
civility.explanation: Characterises the Opposition as living in a 'post-fact environment' rather than rebutting the $13 billion claim on substance.

civility.statement: The fact is it's not our job to go hunting for people. I would recommend that that member goes and hunts for one person in the Labour Party who believes that he's going to last till the election.
civility.explanation: Personal jab about Hipkins' leadership prospects instead of engaging.

civility.statement: Governments who, in the midst of global challenges, decide to double, triple, and quadruple down on their operating allowances and send cost of living payments to dead people and French backpackers are making inflation worse, not better.
civility.explanation: Uses the 'dead people and French backpackers' line to ridicule the previous Government rather than argue neutrally.

civility.statement: Natural gas will play a vital role in energy stability as a low-emission alternative to the coal that was imported by that member's party in the last Government. Until viable, cost-effective, renewable options are in place, we intend to honour our climate change and environmental obligations under this trade agreement.
civility.explanation: Jabs at 'that member's party' for coal imports while making a policy point.

civility.statement: It does feel like the Green Party have used taxpayer money to commission a report to get on TV, from a lawyer that probably is not involved in this agreement.
civility.explanation: Impugns the Greens' motives and the lawyer's credibility rather than engaging the advice's substance.

charisma.statement: ours is a foreign policy of collecting all the facts, hearing all the perspectives, and applying a careful, reasonable, cool-headed approach to the situation—not kneejerk reaction and simplistic moral posturing.
charisma.explanation: Rhetorically confident but defines self against critics rather than building bridges.

charisma.statement: the Middle East is not a situation of black and white; of good and evil; of just one bad actor.
charisma.explanation: Reasoned framing but appeals mainly to those already inclined to 'balance'.

charisma.statement: Those in this House who rush to condemn, or call out, one actor or other, or who demand that the Government do the same, should pause to reflect on whether they are seeking to understand and influence what is going on, or simply virtue-signalling about it.
charisma.explanation: Dismissive of colleagues, shuts down rather than invites.

charisma.statement: We should not accept one set of rules for the powerful and another set of rules for everybody else. We must choose principle, we should choose peace, and we should choose the path of international law.
charisma.explanation: Values-based appeal, rhetorically effective but aimed at those already sympathetic.

charisma.statement: I am absolutely determined, as the Minister for Māori Development, to ensure that the disproportionate statistics that continue to malign Māori iwi, whānau, and other communities are attacked and the inequalities of opportunity and the unequal citizenship implications are addressed.
charisma.explanation: Earnest, inclusive framing of shared concern about inequality.

forthrightness.statement: we note the United States' decision to undertake targeted attacks aimed at degrading Iran's nuclear capabilities was based on the US statement to the UN Security Council that it was acting in collective self-defence consistent with the UN Charter. That was a statement they made, and, of course, in time, that will depend on the emerging evidence.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked directly whether the Government believes the strike meets article 51, he restates the US's own claim and defers to 'emerging evidence' — never gives the Government's view.

forthrightness.statement: we wait till we get the evidence, and we've said it constantly day after day that instead of rushing to judgment, as we were asked this morning by the media: “Has peace broken out?” “No,” we said, “We're going to trust but verify.”
forthrightness.explanation: Repeats the 'trust but verify' line rather than answering whether article 51 permits a pre-emptive strike.

forthrightness.statement: we have not been privy to that information, nor did we, frankly, expect to be, but we have made the wise decision—in my view—to hold our counsel until we know all the facts before we rush to judgment and imperil the future of 5.2 million New Zealanders.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly answers the question of whether NZ received supporting intelligence — no, they have not.

forthrightness.statement: New Zealand is not going to rush to judgment on the lawfulness of various military actions occurring on the other side of the world, arising in such a seriously complex situation, without the full picture.
forthrightness.explanation: Primary-question answer to 'does the Government condemn the strikes' — declines to condemn or explain fully, pivoting to 'not rushing to judgment'.

forthrightness.statement: With the greatest respect, that question just shades into an insult. After all the seriousness that we and Foreign Affairs, working 24/7, have given to this issue over many months and many years, that question is simply a disgraceful insult.
forthrightness.explanation: Refuses to answer whether NZ will rule out joining a US-led war, deflecting by taking offence.

forthrightness.statement: It's not if but when, and when is when we know we'll have the authority legitimately capable of making the claim that they are the representatives of the people.
forthrightness.explanation: On recognising Palestine, gives a conditional 'when, not if' answer but does not commit to inviting the ambassador.

forthrightness.statement: The Regulatory Standards Bill was a matter that was chaperoned through the coalition agreement between ACT and National. That matter is just closing now in select committee, and I look forward to a summary of the robust and strident submissions therein.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked why Te Tiriti was excluded from the bill, he describes process and defers to the select committee rather than answering.

forthrightness.statement: The member has drawn some conclusions that I don't necessarily share with him. And if the member had some time between attending to his various responsibilities up and down the motu, including Te Waipounamu, he will see that there are differences in terms of the coalition arrangements in relation to those bills.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to reconcile opposing the Treaty Principles Bill with backing the Regulatory Standards Bill, he asserts 'differences' without explaining them.

forthrightness.statement: Dairy products have increased in price because the global dairy price has improved—something that is good for New Zealand's farmers.
forthrightness.explanation: Partly answers (explains the price rise) while reframing away from whether households are worse off.

forthrightness.statement: We're now seeing 67 percent approval from the students—actually, they're loving it. Most parents will tell you that if you get, more than two times out of three, your kids loving the lunch you send them, then that's winning. We're doing it for half the price that the previous Government was doing it... we are achieving over 99 percent on-time delivery.
forthrightness.explanation: Pivots from the butter/school-lunch cost question to defending the lunch programme's approval ratings.

forthrightness.statement: Well, if that was true, then it wouldn't, but it's absolutely untrue. Unfortunately, we have an Opposition that lives in a post-fact environment.
forthrightness.explanation: Denies the premise without evidence or figures.

forthrightness.statement: The fact is it's not our job to go hunting for people. I would recommend that that member goes and hunts for one person in the Labour Party who believes that he's going to last till the election.
forthrightness.explanation: Dodges the question about the promised $250 family entirely.

forthrightness.statement: Well, I look at the 12 percent increase in council rates in Wellington, a city that has just built a $2.3 million toilet, and that tells me that this Government is on absolutely the right track when it restricts the range of goals that councils should have.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether various rising costs show the crisis is unfixed, he pivots to attacking council spending.

forthrightness.statement: these included enabling New Zealanders to get 12-month prescriptions for medicines, rather than paying to get a new prescription written every three months; increasing eligibility for rates rebates, for up to 66,000 older New Zealanders; raising the family income threshold for Working for Families
forthrightness.explanation: Directly answers what the Budget cost-of-living initiatives were.

forthrightness.statement: We took a leaf out of the last Government's book, which in one of its rare circumstances decided to target the second and third year of the Best Start payment at those families who actually needed it most, and we have simply continued that targeting into the first year.
forthrightness.explanation: Addresses the Best Start change by justifying the targeting, though doesn't grapple with the $43-per-fortnight loss figure.

forthrightness.statement: this is not a subsidy, and I refer the member to the definition of fossil fuel subsidies in the ACCTS agreement. Article 4.3 of the agreement shows a number of flexibilities to enable New Zealand to address risks to energy security and affordability.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly contests the 'subsidy/breach' claim and gives a basis.

authenticity.statement: We did that in 2003, when Helen Clark and the Labour Government took a principled and courageous stand by opposing the illegal invasion of Iraq.
authenticity.explanation: Ties today's stance to Labour's consistent prior position opposing the Iraq invasion — words matching a long-held record.

authenticity.statement: The Green Party condemns the United States' unlawful and aggressive strikes on Iran, and we call on the Government to do the same.
authenticity.explanation: Consistent with the Greens' long-standing anti-war, pro-international-law positioning.

authenticity.statement: We took a leaf out of the last Government's book, which in one of its rare circumstances decided to target the second and third year of the Best Start payment at those families who actually needed it most, and we have simply continued that targeting into the first year.
authenticity.explanation: Frames the policy as continuous with the prior Government's own approach to defend consistency.

divination.statement: there is no greater motivator—and, again, this refers to the Minister's statements about diplomacy and de-escalation—to obtain nuclear weapons and power than the realised threat of attack by the greatest nuclear power in the world.
divination.explanation: Implicit prediction that the strikes will push Iran toward seeking nuclear weapons — plausible but uncertain.

divination.statement: at the end of the quarter, there are bombs dropping and missiles flying in the Middle East. New Zealand is not immune to these global events... these global events mean it will be very challenging to sustain the previous level of growth into the June quarter.
divination.explanation: Predicts weaker June-quarter growth due to global shocks — plausible and consistent with confidence indicators, but uncertain.

divination.statement: The Reserve Bank, for example, is forecasting positive but subdued growth in the June and September quarters before picking up again strongly at the end of the year.
divination.explanation: Cites RBNZ forecast of subdued-then-strengthening growth; a reasoned but uncertain forecast.

divination.statement: New Zealand will ratify the agreement on 1 July of this year. It will enter into force some time over the next one to two years.
divination.explanation: Forecasts entry into force within one to two years — plausible for a signed trade agreement, timing uncertain.

specificity.statement: A first strike triggers a formal warning, a second means no parole, and a third imposes the maximum sentence without parole.
specificity.explanation: Concrete, precise description of the escalating mechanism of the law — each strike's consequence spelled out.

specificity.statement: Do the crime and they’ll do the time.
specificity.explanation: A slogan; commits to nothing concrete beyond the mechanism already stated.

specificity.statement: Offenders who received valid strike warnings under the 2010 three-strikes regime and whose offences meet the new thresholds will have those strikes recognised and upheld.
specificity.explanation: Names the specific regime (2010) and the condition (meeting new thresholds).

specificity.statement: The focus of Health New Zealand is on timely, quality access to healthcare for all New Zealanders. We have five health targets that we’re focused on, and we want to see them delivering against those targets.
specificity.explanation: References 'five health targets' but supplies no detail relevant to the question asked.

specificity.statement: the Food and Agriculture Organization, an international organisation housed within the broad spectrum of those things that occupy the UN, has given high praise to the sustainability of the New Zealand fishing resource: nigh on 85 percent pass their threshold, reflective of great stewardship, especially over the last 15 months.
specificity.explanation: Cites a figure and source, but the threshold and metric are left vague.

specificity.statement: Recently, the report issued by the Ministry for Primary Industries Situation and Outlook for Primary Industries reflected good news in that part of our fisheries sector, where 13 percent growth—double-digit growth—was recorded in respect of marine farming.
specificity.explanation: Names the report and a concrete figure, though scope/timeframe is loose.

specificity.statement: We are introducing a host of protective measures in the Hauraki Gulf, in the Tīkapa Moana, with a small concession to enable legacy fishermen to continue plying their trade in and around Kawau Island.
specificity.explanation: Names specific locations and a concrete concession, but the 'host of measures' is unenumerated.

specificity.statement: soon we will be bringing back options in the form of proposed legislation to deliver the reforms for the fishing industry, the quota-management system, and a host of other improvements—the most profound since 1986.
specificity.explanation: Names the QMS and a historical benchmark (1986) but the reforms themselves are unspecified and timing is 'soon'.

specificity.statement: In December 2023, 2,936,000 people were employed in New Zealand, and in March 2025, this figure sat at 2,914,000 people, in line with Treasury forecasts.
specificity.explanation: Precise figures and dates for the employment comparison.

specificity.statement: It was always forecast that the unemployment rate would be over 5 percent. It is sitting at 5.1 percent. This is in line with Treasury forecasts, and Treasury are currently forecasting that jobseeker benefit numbers will peak at 217,000 in December 2025.
specificity.explanation: Precise figures, a named forecaster, and a dated peak projection.

specificity.statement: The imprest supply bill seeks authority for the Government to incur a maximum of $39 billion in expenses, $7 billion in capital expenditure, and $1 billion in capital injections.
specificity.explanation: Precise dollar figures for each category of authority sought.

specificity.statement: if our Government hadn’t taken the prudent and responsible step to deliver $23 billion worth of savings in our first Budget, $21 billion worth of savings in our second Budget, and hadn’t taken a number of steps to provide fiscal constraint, then the Government would be in a position of having to ask Parliament for much more money
specificity.explanation: Cites concrete savings figures for two budgets, though the counterfactual is general.

specificity.statement: there isn’t actually a magic money tree; there isn’t a place where the free money comes from. It comes from hard-working people who get up in the morning, go to work
specificity.explanation: A rhetorical framing device rather than a concrete claim or measure.

specificity.statement: the magical money tree seems to give—let’s have a look—$7.25 million to deliver new ministerial suites in the executive wing, at level three. The magical money tree there has $7.25 million, and yet for food banks, those get only $15 million.
specificity.explanation: Cites precise appropriation figures ($7.25m ministerial suites vs $15m food banks) from the Supplementary Estimates.

specificity.statement: The appropriation for emergency housing decreased by $225.79 million to $78.849 million for the 2024-25 year
specificity.explanation: Exact appropriation change and end figure for a named vote line.

specificity.statement: you only have illusory freedom that is not real freedom if you do not have economic freedom—that is, the ability to make meaningful decisions about how you live your life. It is incredibly hard to imagine that any New Zealander could claim to have real freedom if they cannot afford to put food on the table
specificity.explanation: A conceptual argument with an illustrative example but no concrete measures.

specificity.statement: they have cut $16.4 million from services for conservation. They have cut $13.9 million from identification and implementation of protection for natural and historic places. They have cut $6.1 million from managing climate change in Aotearoa New Zealand. They have cut $1.8 million from the Climate Change Commission.
specificity.explanation: A precise, itemised list of cut amounts against named programmes.

specificity.statement: It is not for the 191 New Zealanders who are leaving this country on a plane every single day, three quarters of them between the ages of 18 to 34.
specificity.explanation: Precise figures — 191 per day and an age breakdown — attached to the migration point.

specificity.statement: The primary sector afforded itself $246 million in Sustainable Food and Fibre Futures funds to help on-farm profitability and productivity.
specificity.explanation: Names the fund and a concrete dollar figure and purpose.

specificity.statement: this has afforded $2 million as a contestable fund. I would argue it’s not enough, but it surely speaks to the issues that we face in rural New Zealand.
specificity.explanation: Concrete figure ($2m contestable fund) tied to rural wellbeing/mental health support.

specificity.statement: Throwing money at something doesn’t necessarily mean you’re delivering something and that you’re getting something in return. I’ve seen that a lot of the spending that has happened in the past has been completely and utterly ineffective.
specificity.explanation: No named programme, figure, or example to substantiate the ineffective-spending claim.

specificity.statement: It was really good that we were able to find savings and direct an extra $2 million toward wilding pine control.
specificity.explanation: Concrete figure and named purpose (wilding pine control).

veracity.statement: A first strike triggers a formal warning, a second means no parole, and a third imposes the maximum sentence without parole.
veracity.explanation: Accurate summary of the reinstated three-strikes regime's structure.

veracity.statement: Yes, the law is already being applied to repeat violent offenders, with cases reported in the media just days after it came into force.
veracity.explanation: Plausible and checkable claim about early application; not independently verified here.

veracity.statement: The last Government repealed three strikes to cut prison numbers, even if it meant letting dangerous offenders walk free.
veracity.explanation: The repeal is factual, but 'letting dangerous offenders walk free' imputes a motive/effect that is contestable and misleading.

veracity.statement: I’m very happy to talk about Nelson Hospital and the fact that the rescoping started when she was the Minister—when she was the Minister. We are actually going to get on and deliver it, unlike the fake promise made in 2020 by the former Government, where they said spades would be in the ground by 2023—not a spade even got near Nelson.
veracity.explanation: The 2020 'spades by 2023' claim and non-delivery are checkable; 'not a spade even got near' is likely hyperbolic.

veracity.statement: which party was it that put the charge on in terms of pharmaceutical prescriptions in the first place when they were told by their colleagues in New Zealand First not to do it and now it’s being defended by that very Minister over there—has she got no memory?
veracity.explanation: The claim that Labour introduced the prescription charge over NZ First's objection is a checkable historical assertion.

veracity.statement: Recently, the report issued by the Ministry for Primary Industries Situation and Outlook for Primary Industries reflected good news in that part of our fisheries sector, where 13 percent growth—double-digit growth—was recorded in respect of marine farming.
veracity.explanation: Specific, sourced growth figure attributed to a named MPI report; checkable.

veracity.explanation: Specific, checkable official statistics; presented as tracking Treasury forecasts.

veracity.explanation: Specific unemployment figure (5.1%) and Treasury forecast attribution; checkable.

veracity.statement: The imprest supply bill seeks authority for the Government to incur a maximum of $39 billion in expenses, $7 billion in capital expenditure, and $1 billion in capital injections.
veracity.explanation: Concrete, checkable figures from the bill being debated.

veracity.statement: if our Government hadn’t taken the prudent and responsible step to deliver $23 billion worth of savings in our first Budget, $21 billion worth of savings in our second Budget, and hadn’t taken a number of steps to provide fiscal constraint, then the Government would be in a position of having to ask Parliament for much more money
veracity.explanation: Savings figures are checkable but 'savings' framing is contestable; directionally supportable.

veracity.statement: It delivered the worst cost of living crisis in a generation, from which many households are yet to recover. It delivered masses of debt, a huge spike in inflation, and price rises.
veracity.explanation: Inflation spike and cost-of-living pressures are real, but 'worst in a generation' and sole attribution to the prior government are hyperbolic and omit global causes.

veracity.statement: This Government is continuing to build more State houses, to build more classrooms, to deliver hospitals. For the member to claim in his supplementary question that that is not the case has the potential to mislead the House.
veracity.explanation: A contested factual claim countering Andersen's; both sides assert opposing facts on construction, so accuracy is unresolved from the text.

veracity.statement: we had high tradeable inflation during the period when we were in Government—particularly post-COVID—because there was a global pandemic and because there were supply chain issues. If you look at the data around tradeable versus non-tradeable inflation, you will see the major difference
veracity.explanation: The tradeable/non-tradeable inflation distinction and post-COVID supply shocks are accurate, though it downplays domestic contributors.

veracity.statement: the magical money tree seems to give—let’s have a look—$7.25 million to deliver new ministerial suites in the executive wing, at level three. The magical money tree there has $7.25 million, and yet for food banks, those get only $15 million.
veracity.explanation: The figures appear checkable, but juxtaposing very different appropriations for rhetorical contrast is somewhat misleading about relative priorities.

veracity.statement: The appropriation for emergency housing decreased by $225.79 million to $78.849 million for the 2024-25 year
veracity.explanation: Precise figures drawn from the Treasury Supplementary Estimates briefing; checkable.

veracity.statement: this Government has tanked the economy.
veracity.explanation: Sweeping, hyperbolic characterisation not supported by the mixed growth/recession picture she herself describes.

veracity.statement: they have cut $16.4 million from services for conservation. They have cut $13.9 million from identification and implementation of protection for natural and historic places. They have cut $6.1 million from managing climate change in Aotearoa New Zealand. They have cut $1.8 million from the Climate Change Commission.
veracity.explanation: Specific, checkable appropriation figures; accuracy plausible though framing as 'cuts' may omit reprioritisation context.

veracity.statement: The Prime Minister and the Associate Minister of Housing had the gall to stand in front of TV cameras in January of this year and announce that the Government had met its targets early to kick people out of emergency housing, when, in December last year, they had received a briefing that said that homelessness was visibly increasing in our major centres.
veracity.explanation: The January announcement and December briefing are specific checkable events; 'kick people out' is a loaded gloss on the policy.

veracity.statement: It is not for the 191 New Zealanders who are leaving this country on a plane every single day, three quarters of them between the ages of 18 to 34.
veracity.explanation: A concrete, checkable migration statistic, though net vs gross departure framing may be selective.

veracity.statement: this was actually identified just two weeks ago in a report from the International Monetary Fund ...
