On provisional figures for 2025, there has been a 30 percent increase in domestic students enrolling in initial teacher education for the first time.
specificity.explanation: Multiple precise figures, dates, and a clear benchmark (“since records began in 2009”).

specificity.statement: The teacher retention rate for secondary school teachers in New Zealand is 90 percent, which is unchanged from years and years, but the important thing is that the numbers do not lie—as I said in my primary question, a 30 percent increase in the first-time enrolments of domestic students in 2025.
specificity.explanation: Cites specific retention and enrolment figures.

specificity.statement: Over the last year, Gumboot Friday has been able to scale up and deliver more than 30,000 free counselling sessions and has supported more than 10,000 young Kiwis who might not otherwise have access to timely support.
specificity.explanation: Concrete counts of sessions delivered and young people supported over a defined period.

specificity.statement: Funding for 2025-26 will deliver up to 40,000 individual counselling sessions, reaching as many as 15,000 young Kiwis.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete target figures and the funding year.

specificity.statement: What I can assure the House is that last year the average rates increase in this country was 9.6 percent and the inflation rate was 2.2 percent.
specificity.explanation: Two precise figures directly contrasting rates rises against inflation.

specificity.statement: Well, it is fixing a water pipe. What is non-core? Well, spending $17,000 to paint a statue of a doughnut in Selwyn—non-core.
specificity.explanation: Concrete dollar figure and example illustrating the core/non-core distinction.

specificity.statement: This Government is on the side of ratepayers who are sick and tired of seeing their councils spending on nice-to-haves. They must address the basics.
specificity.explanation: “Nice-to-haves” and “the basics” are undefined generalities.

specificity.statement: I am certainly aware that the number of people working at Radio New Zealand increased dramatically after 2017, from about 265 through to about 365—so over 100—and there may be some reversal of that flow, but there will still be a lot more people there than there were some time ago, and they are delivering a great job for New Zealanders.
specificity.explanation: Gives approximate but concrete staffing figures and a timeframe.

specificity.statement: Costs have increased between 2019 and 2023 by some 40 percent, and we’re doing something about it. Recently, the Government announced that we would remove the rigid aspect of the insulation rules to ease the burden on builders, thereby lowering costs without lowering standards.
specificity.explanation: Gives a cost-increase figure and timeframe plus a named mechanism (insulation rule change), though “rigid aspect” is loosely defined.

specificity.statement: By official estimates, the changes are expected to lower building costs by up to $15,000 per new build.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete dollar figure and its source, though “up to” limits the commitment.

specificity.statement: Does she believe teachers deserve a pay offer that reflects the hard work that they do; if so, how is the lowest pay offer in 30 years even close to enough?
specificity.explanation: References a concrete comparative claim (lowest offer in 30 years) but no figures for the offer itself.

specificity.statement: how has the Government’s declining of 28 percent more emergency housing applications in March 2025 compared to the year before contributed to the Auckland, Far North, and Whangārei territorial authorities reporting the highest number of homeless whānau in Aotearoa according to the Homelessness insights report June 2025?
specificity.explanation: Cites a specific percentage, month, named regions, and the source report.

civility.statement: Point of order, Mr Speaker. Are you telling this House that your statement is constitutional authority now for the ruling you just gave—yes or no?
civility.explanation: Confrontational demand aimed at the Speaker; harsh in tone though it targets the ruling's basis rather than a personal characteristic.

civility.statement: Given that there was a massive injection of funding between 2018 and 2023 and, despite that, Morning Report and RNZ have gone from No. 1 in the market in the last five years to No. 8, is it capable of being salvaged or is it just plain hopeless?
civility.explanation: Loaded, sensationalised framing (“plain hopeless”) that denigrates the outfit rather than engaging its performance constructively.

civility.statement: Well, the last Government banned the exploration of oil and gas. It set out an objective for 100 percent renewable energy that made it hard for generators to see that they should be investing in electricity generation that used gas or coal, and then they threatened a huge white elephant in the form of Lake Onslow that actively stopped people investing in electricity generation.
civility.explanation: Sharp criticism of the previous government's policy decisions, but stays on policy rather than personal attack.

civility.statement: You can play with sound bites; we play with substance.
civility.explanation: A dismissive rhetorical put-down of opponents, though mild and not a personal insult.

civility.statement: Well, there is no question that rising electricity prices are a challenge for many New Zealanders. That is a facile observation. A deeper observation is to ask: why is that?
civility.explanation: Acknowledges the underlying hardship but the “facile observation” aside is a mild swipe at the questioner's line.

civility.statement: As mentioned previously this week, this Government takes homelessness—particularly living without shelter—very seriously, and I acknowledge that the homelessness rate and living without shelter went up between 2018 and 2023 despite serious spending.
civility.explanation: Concedes the problem's scale and takes it seriously; a respectful, substance-focused opening.

civility.statement: We’re absolutely disgusted by the number of children and others living in these dank, dark, dangerous, squalid motels throughout the country, and that’s why I’m very proud that we now have 3,000 less children in those motels and hotels compared to when we first came into administration.
civility.explanation: Strong emotive language (“dank, dark, dangerous, squalid”) attacks the previous approach's conditions rather than a person.

civility.statement: That’s the first I’ve heard of that specific example, and I’m very concerned if indeed that allegation is proven to be accurate.
civility.explanation: Measured, respectful response to a serious allegation without dismissing it.

civility.statement: We are very agile in our response to the current concerns. We’ve directed our teams to get out there and understand where we can accelerate some targeted interventions, to liaise with some of the leaders whose names the member opposite has mentioned, and to ensure that we have an enduring solution and not one that relies on outbursts rather than outcomes and exclamations rather than execution.
civility.explanation: The “outbursts rather than outcomes and exclamations rather than execution” line is a rhetorical dig at the opposition's approach rather than engagement with substance.

civility.statement: I certainly can reflect on the $1.5 billion or so that was thrown into emergency housing, hurting people throughout the country, and yet emergency houses went up for a very, very long time under the previous Government.
civility.explanation: Loaded language (“thrown into,” “hurting people”) criticises the prior approach in charged terms.

civility.statement: Why did the Government plough ahead with their changes to emergency housing, when they were explicitly warned by the ministry that it would “create a risk of increased levels of rough sleeping, people living in cars, and overcrowding”, which we are now seeing?
civility.explanation: Pointed but policy-focused challenge grounded in the ministry's own advice.

civility.statement: Well, it is fixing a water pipe. What is non-core? Well, spending $17,000 to paint a statue of a doughnut in Selwyn—non-core.
civility.explanation: Uses a mocking specific example to ridicule council spending; a swipe at a council's choices rather than a personal attack.

civility.statement: I do not accept the premise of that quote. This Government is one that is invested in the needs of local communities and was elected with a clear mandate to get councils back to basics.
civility.explanation: Disagrees on the merits without attacking the mayor personally.

civility.statement: I am certainly aware that the number of people working at Radio New Zealand increased dramatically after 2017, from about 265 through to about 365—so over 100—and there may be some reversal of that flow, but there will still be a lot more people there than there were some time ago, and they are delivering a great job for New Zealanders.
civility.explanation: Acknowledges RNZ is “delivering a great job” even while defending cuts — respectful toward the affected organisation.

civility.statement: I find listening to Morning Report highly motivational, and I do it most days. All politicians will have a variety of opinions on that, but I’ve got every confidence that Radio New Zealand can continue to deliver a high-quality service.
civility.explanation: Responds to a “plain hopeless” framing with a respectful defence of RNZ rather than a counter-attack.

civility.statement: I do thank the member and the Labour Party for their support of that in the spirit of bipartisanship, and I encourage them to continue on in that vein.
civility.explanation: Gracious, bridge-building acknowledgement of an opponent's constructive contribution.

civility.statement: Who is right, front-line community service providers who say the cost of living is getting worse, or Christopher Luxon, who said a year ago, and confirmed again yesterday, that the cost of living is getting under control?
civility.explanation: Pointed policy challenge that quotes the PM's own words rather than attacking him personally.

civility.statement: Does she believe teachers deserve a pay offer that reflects the hard work that they do; if so, how is the lowest pay offer in 30 years even close to enough?
civility.explanation: Challenges the pay offer on the merits; “lowest in 30 years” is a sharp but policy-focused framing.

civility.statement: There is a long and consistent history of Speakers ensuring that Ministers do not ask questions of those who are asking questions of them. Their role in question time is to respond to questions, not propose them.
civility.explanation: Raises a procedural point respectfully and impersonally, focused on process not the individual.

charisma.statement: Point of order, Mr Speaker. Are you telling this House that your statement is constitutional authority now for the ruling you just gave—yes or no?
charisma.explanation: Combative, cornering rhetoric with no attempt to persuade or find common ground.

charisma.statement: You can play with sound bites; we play with substance.
charisma.explanation: Us-vs-them jab that draws a dividing line rather than persuading or building consensus.

charisma.statement: Well, there is no question that rising electricity prices are a challenge for many New Zealanders. That is a facile observation. A deeper observation is to ask: why is that?
charisma.explanation: Concedes a shared concern before pivoting, but the framing appeals mainly to her own side.

charisma.statement: Well, it can be the case that something is both improving but it still hasn’t improved enough. That is our position.
charisma.explanation: A measured, honest framing that could bridge, but still defends her own side's line.

charisma.statement: We are very agile in our response to the current concerns. We’ve directed our teams to get out there and understand where we can accelerate some targeted interventions, to liaise with some of the leaders whose names the member opposite has mentioned, and to ensure that we have an enduring solution and not one that relies on outbursts rather than outcomes and exclamations rather than execution.
charisma.explanation: Alliterative attack framing that rallies his own side rather than seeking common ground.

charisma.statement: Just as they grabbed Phar Lap and our pavlova, it’s proved to be the same with “Everyone Must Go”.
charisma.explanation: Light, good-humoured trans-Tasman quip that entertains, though it appeals mainly to a domestic audience.

charisma.statement: This Government is on the side of ratepayers who are sick and tired of seeing their councils spending on nice-to-haves. They must address the basics.
charisma.explanation: Populist “on the side of ratepayers” framing that rallies a constituency against councils rather than bridging.

charisma.statement: I find listening to Morning Report highly motivational, and I do it most days. All politicians will have a variety of opinions on that, but I’ve got every confidence that Radio New Zealand can continue to deliver a high-quality service.
charisma.explanation: Disarms a hostile question with self-deprecating good humour and an even-handed nod, lowering the temperature.

charisma.statement: I do thank the member and the Labour Party for their support of that in the spirit of bipartisanship, and I encourage them to continue on in that vein.
charisma.explanation: Explicitly acknowledges and thanks the opposition for cross-party cooperation, inviting continued common ground.

forthrightness.statement: In December 2022, food price inflation was 10.7 percent. In March 2023, food price inflation was 11.3 percent. In June 2023, food price inflation was 12.3 percent. Since being elected, our Government achieved, in the March 2024 quarter, 2.4 percent food price inflation; in June 2024, 0.2 percent; in September 2024, 0.7 percent—I can go on.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked specifically when the price of butter would come down, she answered with general food-inflation figures and never addressed butter or a timeframe.

forthrightness.statement: Well, it can be the case that something is both improving but it still hasn’t improved enough. That is our position.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to adjudicate between providers and the PM, she gives a genuine nuanced position rather than dodging, though she doesn't pick a side outright.

forthrightness.statement: As mentioned previously this week, this Government takes homelessness—particularly living without shelter—very seriously, and I acknowledge that the homelessness rate and living without shelter went up between 2018 and 2023 despite serious spending.
forthrightness.explanation: Acknowledges the trend but leans on a report caveat rather than directly answering why the rejection rate grew eightfold.

forthrightness.statement: I’ll repeat this again just for the member’s benefit: “It is not possible to determine the extent to which changes described in this report … are attributable to policy changes.”
forthrightness.explanation: Faced with specific rough-sleeping percentage increases and a direct causal question, he repeats a report caveat instead of engaging the figures.

forthrightness.statement: That’s the first I’ve heard of that specific example, and I’m very concerned if indeed that allegation is proven to be accurate.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly says he hadn't heard the example and expresses concern, but doesn't answer whether he'd reverse the criteria.

forthrightness.statement: I absolutely am. I will stand by the statement and I’ll stand by it for many, many years. I stand by supporting the young lady in Tauranga that I visited, who had four children in emergency housing between 2019 and 2022, and establishing the Priority One decision-making process that enabled her to actually get into a social house.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly affirms he stands by the statement and justifies it, though it slides into a list of achievements.

forthrightness.statement: The 84 percent figure is accurate and was calculated by the Ministry of Health based on Tōtara Hospice’s most recently published annual report from their website. I’ve been advised this is a much higher amount than the average 50-55 percent of funding for hospices across New Zealand.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly stands by the figure and explains its basis (the ministry's calculation from the annual report) rather than dodging.

forthrightness.statement: But, look, I acknowledge we need to have a nationally consistent approach to palliative care throughout New Zealand. It is inconsistent. This is a piece of work which is a priority for me, and I’ve asked Health New Zealand to progress it.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked why he's disputing the hospice's accounts with its CEO, he pivots to the broader consistency-of-funding work rather than the specific dispute.

forthrightness.statement: In regard to the second part of the question, the negotiation is an operational matter. It is being undertaken by the Public Service Commissioner. I agree with his comment that the offer was carefully crafted to recognise the contribution of teachers while ensuring affordability for taxpayers.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked how a 1% annual offer “backs and strengthens” teachers, she deflects to it being an operational matter for the Commissioner rather than defending the figure.

forthrightness.statement: I do not accept the premise of that quote. This Government is one that is invested in the needs of local communities and was elected with a clear mandate to get councils back to basics.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly rejects the mayor's premise and states his own position, though he doesn't engage the substance of central-government stepping up.

forthrightness.statement: Well, I wouldn’t give the member the exact number, but there have been substantial job losses, as everybody is aware, across the media sector.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked directly how many people have lost jobs in the media sector since he became Minister, he explicitly declines to give the number.

divination.statement: In the short term, this means jobs for people and good incomes. In the longer term, it means better infrastructure and better living standards for everyone.
divination.explanation: Predicts jobs and improved living standards from the infrastructure agenda; plausible in direction but vague and unfalsifiable as stated.

divination.statement: Funding for 2025-26 will deliver up to 40,000 individual counselling sessions, reaching as many as 15,000 young Kiwis.
divination.explanation: Forecasts next-year delivery of up to 40,000 sessions/15,000 young people; plausible given the prior year's 30,000/10,000, but “up to” makes it a ceiling rather than a firm prediction.

divination.statement: By official estimates, the changes are expected to lower building costs by up to $15,000 per new build.
divination.explanation: Forecasts savings of “up to $15,000” per build; the “up to” ceiling and reliance on official estimates make it plausible but unproven.

strength.statement: In education, for example, the smart use of standardised designs and off-site manufacturing has reduced the average cost of a new classroom from about $1.2 million to $620,000.
strength.explanation: Claims a delivered cost reduction with a mechanism, indicating follow-through rather than mere announcement.

strength.statement: We’re absolutely disgusted by the number of children and others living in these dank, dark, dangerous, squalid motels throughout the country, and that’s why I’m very proud that we now have 3,000 less children in those motels and hotels compared to when we first came into administration.
strength.explanation: Claims a concrete delivered outcome (3,000 fewer children in motels) attributable to the Government's actions, indicating follow-through.

strength.statement: I absolutely am. I will stand by the statement and I’ll stand by it for many, many years. I stand by supporting the young lady in Tauranga that I visited, who had four children in emergency housing between 2019 and 2022, and establishing the Priority One decision-making process that enabled her to actually get into a social house.
strength.explanation: Points to a specific policy mechanism enacted to deliver housing, though evidence of broad follow-through is anecdotal.

strength.statement: But, look, I acknowledge we need to have a nationally consistent approach to palliative care throughout New Zealand. It is inconsistent. This is a piece of work which is a priority for me, and I’ve asked Health New Zealand to progress it.
strength.explanation: States a priority and a directive to officials, but describes work commissioned rather than delivered.

strength.statement: Tourism New Zealand’s stats show that this initiative delivered an addition 7,981 visitors, which is exceeding the initial forecasts. These additional visitors generated an estimated $22 million in visitor spending to our economy.
strength.explanation: Claims measurable delivered results from a policy the Government funded and ran.

strength.statement: The schooling teacher workforce grew by 2.5 percent in 2024, delivering 1,864 new teachers, the largest year-on-year increase since records began in 2009. On provisional figures for 2025, there has been a 30 percent increase in domestic students enrolling in initial teacher education for the first time.
strength.explanation: Points to delivered workforce growth as evidence of backing educators, indicating follow-through beyond announcement.

strength.statement: Over the last year, Gumboot Friday has been able to scale up and deliver more than 30,000 free counselling sessions and has supported more than 10,000 young Kiwis who might not otherwise have access to timely support.
strength.explanation: Ties a funded commitment ($24m over four years) to concrete first-year delivery figures, indicating follow-through.

strength.statement: Costs have increased between 2019 and 2023 by some 40 percent, and we’re doing something about it. Recently, the Government announced that we would remove the rigid aspect of the insulation rules to ease the burden on builders, thereby lowering costs without lowering standards.
strength.explanation: Describes an announced change rather than a delivered outcome; follow-through still prospective.

authenticity.statement: I absolutely am. I will stand by the statement and I’ll stand by it for many, many years. I stand by supporting the young lady in Tauranga that I visited, who had four children in emergency housing between 2019 and 2022, and establishing the Priority One decision-making process that enabled her to actually get into a social house.
authenticity.explanation: Backs the stated commitment with a concrete named process (Priority One) and case example, showing some alignment of words and actions, though the individual anecdote is hard to generalise.

civility.statement: Israel's military response to the events of 7 October 2023 long ago ceased to be proportionate, reasonable, or moral, and because Hamas continues to act with complete disregard for civilian life.
civility.explanation: Harsh but even-handed criticism directed at the conduct of both Israel and Hamas, not at individuals; policy/conduct focused.

civility.statement: Sometimes, it pays to be patient and find out the facts before shouting from the rooftops.
civility.explanation: A mild implicit rebuke of critics rather than a personal attack.

civility.statement: Whilst there are both sides of the story occupant in New Zealand, we hope they haven't brought their politics with them—that they remember that this country is a peaceful country, it has got its values, there's a flag to salute, there's our laws to be obeyed, and there's a political system and freedom that needs to be subscribed to, including the freedom of religion.
civility.explanation: Implies NZ's Palestinian/diaspora communities may import conflict and not obey laws, an othering insinuation rather than substantive engagement.

civility.statement: Who said that? You must have come down the last shower.
civility.explanation: A dismissive personal jibe at an interjector rather than engagement with the point made.

civility.statement: to liken the invasion of, first of all, Georgia, then Crimea, then Ukraine to 7 October and the Hamas terrorism is an extraordinary juxtaposition of history and fact.
civility.explanation: Sharp but directed at the argument's logic, not the person.

civility.statement: are we just virtue signalling? Virtue signalling is not what we're going to do here.
civility.explanation: Frames opponents' proposed measures as mere 'virtue signalling', a dismissive characterisation.

civility.statement: why didn't he mention the infrastructure work for our no-nonsense Cook Strait ferry programme that starts later this year— saving the taxpayer billions of dollars, in stark contrast, sausage roll eater, to the profligate mess we inherited?
civility.explanation: 'Sausage roll eater' is a personal jibe and 'profligate mess' is a partisan swipe within an otherwise substantive interjection.

civility.statement: if I have to rely upon that questioner for support, my party would be truly desperate.
civility.explanation: A jab at Waititi delivered within a point of order rather than substantive engagement.

civility.statement: The Labour Party welcomes the ministerial statement from this Government on very concerning matters in Gaza. We want to be very clear and upfront that we continue to be concerned with what's transpiring across the entire Middle East region. We know, though, that action speaks louder than words.
civility.explanation: Constructive, welcomes the Government's statement before raising differences.

civility.statement: We welcome the Government's recent steps, sanctions against Israeli Ministers, and co-signing a joint international statement calling for an end to the war. But we must be honest: these moves come after 24 other countries have already taken action.
civility.explanation: Credits the Government's steps while making a factual criticism about timing.

civility.statement: Gaza is starving. Israel is deliberately engineering a famine. They blockade thousands and thousands of trucks that have lined up at the Rafah border. Food has been stockpiled in warehouses—in fact, enough food that could replenish the whole of Gaza for three months. Supply-ready, systems-ready, but they are being denied entry.
civility.explanation: Harsh but aimed at state conduct rather than an individual.

civility.statement: This Government does many cruel things, but nothing is as cruel as being mates with those committing this genocide. They are complicit—for Israel to not open the gates.
civility.explanation: Accuses the Government of cruelty and complicity in genocide—a character/motive attack, not policy critique.

civility.statement: We do not accept this Government's pathetic lip-service calling for a ceasefire. It's your fifth time in two years.
civility.explanation: 'Pathetic lip-service' is a dismissive characterisation, though 'fifth time in two years' is a factual jab.

civility.statement: We need strong sanctions—expulsion of the Israel ambassador, as we have called for in the past. We don't need whaiwhai pīhau solutions, which means following the flatulence of others like the US. We must lead with courage and humanity.
civility.explanation: 'Following the flatulence of others' is a colourful sneer at foreign-policy alignment.

civility.statement: I find it troubling when I'm misrepresented in this House. I did not say that. I said up to 130,000 families could benefit. You know what? We've got lots of years in office left to go, so I'm confident that might happen.
civility.explanation: Pushes back on being misrepresented without a personal attack.

civility.statement: So I say to every family in New Zealand with kids in early childhood education: get online and apply. Our Government wants you to have that money in your bank account. Barbara Edmonds and Chris Hipkins would take it from you.
civility.explanation: 'Would take it from you' misrepresents opponents' position as wanting to remove the benefit.

civility.statement: Does she accept that her Government does not have a plan to get unemployment rates to zero percent, and, if so, does she think unemployed people deserve to live in poverty?
civility.explanation: A loaded question implying the Minister thinks the unemployed deserve poverty; more of a rhetorical trap than substantive.

civility.statement: How is it in order to refuse to answer a question and then immediately go into attacking the person who asked it? It's a very straightforward question: how many people received the full benefit of a promise that he made them? He could answer it or he could not answer it, but pivoting straight into an attack on the Opposition is just a bit desperate.
civility.explanation: Legitimate procedural objection, though 'a bit desperate' adds a mild jab.

civility.statement: How many blocks of butter can he buy for the $60 a week he claims to spend on groceries?
civility.explanation: A pointed 'gotcha' aimed at the PM's personal grocery-spend claim rather than a policy substance.

civility.statement: if he wants to put a specific question on notice, feel free to do so. But the great news here is that this is a Government that supports low and middle income working New Zealanders, the people the Labour Party purported to care about but don't care about any more.
civility.explanation: 'Purported to care ... but don't care about any more' impugns opponents' motives.

civility.statement: Absolutely. What FamilyBoost is about—for the member, so that he understands it—is that depending upon your income and depending upon your costs, everyone receives their full entitlement.
civility.explanation: 'So that he understands it' is a mildly condescending aside.

civility.statement: it was his Government that created out-of-control spending, tripled the debt three times, ended up rising inflation, throwing interest rates through the absolute roof.
civility.explanation: Partisan blame aimed at the previous government's record.

civility.statement: Well, it's a smart-arse question, isn't it? But I will just say to you: that member is supposed to be the Leader of the Opposition, and in Opposition, you oppose but you also propose. There's no proposals from that side.
civility.explanation: Labels the question 'smart-arse' and dismisses the questioner rather than engaging.

civility.statement: 100 additional medical training places have been added over the term of this Government across the University of Auckland and the University of Otago. We're also cutting red tape so international doctors can work here more easily. While others talked, we're delivering.
civility.explanation: 'While others talked, we're delivering' is a partisan swipe.

charisma.statement: Israel's military response to the events of 7 October 2023 long ago ceased to be proportionate, reasonable, or moral, and because Hamas continues to act with complete disregard for civilian life.
charisma.explanation: Balanced framing that assigns blame to both sides rather than rallying one side against the other.

charisma.statement: it is an awful long way away from New Zealand, and we have the right to feel awfully frustrated that for decades of all of our lives, this issue has been there, at the centre of international news.
charisma.explanation: Appeals to shared weariness rather than building consensus toward action.

charisma.statement: Whilst there are both sides of the story occupant in New Zealand, we hope they haven't brought their politics with them—that they remember that this country is a peaceful country, it has got its values, there's a flag to salute, there's our laws to be obeyed, and there's a political system and freedom that needs to be subscribed to, including the freedom of religion.
charisma.explanation: Alienating toward the very diaspora communities the question was about; not consensus-building.

charisma.statement: are we just virtue signalling? Virtue signalling is not what we're going to do here.
charisma.explanation: Rallying his own position by belittling the alternative rather than persuading.

charisma.statement: The Labour Party welcomes the ministerial statement from this Government on very concerning matters in Gaza. We want to be very clear and upfront that we continue to be concerned with what's transpiring across the entire Middle East region. We know, though, that action speaks louder than words.
charisma.explanation: Bipartisan tone acknowledging common concern before criticism.

charisma.statement: Silence is no longer the issue; inaction is. If we believe in international law and human rights, we must act with moral clarity and urgency.
charisma.explanation: A rousing appeal to shared values to spur action.

charisma.statement: I acknowledge the statement, but we need to have more than words—we need to have more than words. We are beyond the point where we need to have action.
charisma.explanation: Emphatic call to action but appeals largely to those already sympathetic.

charisma.statement: I was helping a family get their grandmother over so she could help with their children—they had come from Gaza—and she was here for one week before the bombs dropped on her apartment, destroying the apartment that she lived in. This is a family now living in New Zealand. Gaza might be far away, but it is also close as well.
charisma.explanation: Personal narrative used to draw the House toward a shared human concern.

charisma.statement: This Government does many cruel things, but nothing is as cruel as being mates with those committing this genocide. They are complicit—for Israel to not open the gates.
charisma.explanation: Us-vs-them condemnation that alienates rather than persuades the Government benches.

charisma.statement: We need strong sanctions—expulsion of the Israel ambassador, as we have called for in the past. We don't need whaiwhai pīhau solutions, which means following the flatulence of others like the US. We must lead with courage and humanity.
charisma.explanation: Stirring to supporters but combative toward the Government and allies.

charisma.statement: So I say to every family in New Zealand with kids in early childhood education: get online and apply. Our Government wants you to have that money in your bank account. Barbara Edmonds and Chris Hipkins would take it from you.
charisma.explanation: Direct appeal to families, but pivots to a partisan attack that alienates opponents.

veracity.statement: Israel's military response to the events of 7 October 2023 long ago ceased to be proportionate, reasonable, or moral, and because Hamas continues to act with complete disregard for civilian life.
veracity.explanation: A broadly defensible characterisation of the situation, though 'proportionate/moral' are contestable value-laden judgements.

veracity.statement: This New Zealand Government has designated the entirety of Hamas, whose standard objectives include the complete destruction of Israel, a terrorist organisation.
veracity.explanation: Accurate: NZ did extend its terrorist designation to the whole of Hamas.

veracity.statement: We have also put in place travel bans against Israeli Ministers who have taken complete steps to undermine the two-State solution by advocating illegal settlements and settler violence.

forthrightness.statement: I did not make that promise. What I said—and I've gone and checked the transcript—is that, at the time that I was asked by journalists at our initial briefing on FamilyBoost how many families we thought would get the maximum entitlement, I said, "I can confirm that based on official modelling, around 21,000 families would be entitled to that payment." Now, the point is this: first of all, I based that statement on the modelling that had been provided to me in good faith by IRD and, second of all, there is a difference that I encourage the member to contemplate between a maximum payment and a full payment.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly addresses the '21,000 families' charge and explains the maximum-vs-full distinction.

forthrightness.statement: In Budget 2024, we delivered meaningful tax relief, an increased in-work tax credit, and the FamilyBoost childcare rebate. Further initiatives such as Working for Families in Budget 2025 are helping to ease financial pressure for families across the country.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether she agrees with the report's findings; pivots to listing Government initiatives rather than engaging the report.

forthrightness.statement: No, I completely refute that. If you look at where the Government has focused its effort around housing, around incomes, and around food, which are all related to the cost of living pressure, we've got a plan and we're sticking to it.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to accept the report's specific finding that outcomes worsened 2024–26; denies flatly and gestures at 'a plan' without addressing the finding.

forthrightness.statement: the good news with FamilyBoost—a policy that he and his party did not support—is that we have 62,000 families that have received payments to support them on their early childcare education costs. The changes that the Minister has made to expand the threshold and also the coverage means that there's another 22,000 families and households that can participate in early childhood cost subsidisation.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked specifically how many families received the $250/fortnight; cites total families assisted instead, not the figure asked.

forthrightness.statement: if he wants to put a specific question on notice, feel free to do so. But the great news here is that this is a Government that supports low and middle income working New Zealanders, the people the Labour Party purported to care about but don't care about any more.
forthrightness.explanation: Declines to give the number asked and pivots to a partisan attack.

forthrightness.statement: Absolutely. What FamilyBoost is about—for the member, so that he understands it—is that depending upon your income and depending upon your costs, everyone receives their full entitlement.
forthrightness.explanation: Reframes 'full entitlement' rather than confirming how many got the $250, sidestepping the substance.

forthrightness.statement: Well, it's a smart-arse question, isn't it? But I will just say to you: that member is supposed to be the Leader of the Opposition, and in Opposition, you oppose but you also propose. There's no proposals from that side.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked how many blocks of butter $60 buys; does not engage the point at all.

forthrightness.statement: I'm very proud of the work that we've done to support our seniors across New Zealand, and I want to thank the New Zealand First party, in particular. As you saw at the last Budget, there is a rates rebate for 60,000 gold card holders that need support with their rates payments.
forthrightness.explanation: Responsive to the SuperGold question, affirming its value and citing a related measure.

forthrightness.statement: The Regulatory Standards Bill is really about ensuring we have better-quality regulations so we don't add compliance costs and therefore drive up inflation, which makes the cost of living difficult for people.
forthrightness.explanation: Addresses the bill's purpose but does not directly answer whether it could affect SuperGold entitlements.

forthrightness.statement: that is not the intent of the legislation that is currently before the Finance and Expenditure Committee. That legislation seeks only to give the courts a discretion to come to a fair and equitable decision relating to that litigation.
forthrightness.explanation: Addresses the intent but does not directly confirm/deny that banks would avoid paying the debt.

forthrightness.statement: One of the pieces of legislation that this coalition Government has passed is the Customer and Product Data Act earlier this year. It was finally passed in March of this year. Now, that is a piece of legislation that enables for what is often referred to as open banking.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether his talk has helped with electricity prices; pivots to open-banking legislation.

forthrightness.statement: the member will know that I am conflicted on matters relating to groceries and supermarkets, and so I will defer answers on those matters to the Hon Nicola Willis.
forthrightness.explanation: Declines to answer the butter-price question, though for a stated conflict-of-interest reason.

authenticity.statement: We have always said, this Government, that it's not a matter of if but when, but the question that has to be answered, saving us lowering our standards of statehood, is who would we negotiate with? Who would we talk to? Who would establish the State sans or without an election?
authenticity.explanation: 'Not if but when' is consistent with the Government's repeated stated position.

authenticity.statement: Labour's position has been clear: we support an immediate and permanent ceasefire and the unimpeded flow of humanitarian aid and, of course, a two-State solution. We continue to denounce the actions of Hamas and will continue to do so into the future.
authenticity.explanation: States a consistent, longstanding party position and applies it even-handedly (denouncing Hamas).

authenticity.statement: We have delivered the scheme exactly according to the eligibility criteria we outlined in our campaign. In fact, more recently, we have gone further and made the scheme more generous so that now families can get up to 40 percent rebates on their early childhood fees, and families on higher incomes are now eligible for the scheme.
authenticity.explanation: Claims delivery matches the campaign promise; defensible on scheme design but contested given far fewer families got the maximum than modelled.

authenticity.statement: I did not make that promise. What I said—and I've gone and checked the transcript—is that, at the time that I was asked by journalists at our initial briefing on FamilyBoost how many families we thought would get the maximum entitlement, I said, "I can confirm that based on official modelling, around 21,000 families would be entitled to that payment." Now, the point is this: first of all, I based that statement on the modelling that had been provided to me in good faith by IRD and, second of all, there is a difference that I encourage the member to contemplate between a maximum payment and a full payment.
authenticity.explanation: Defends consistency by parsing 'entitled' vs 'promised', a fine but arguable distinction.

divination.statement: The current uptick in annual CPI inflation is expected to extend into the September quarter of this year but not persist beyond that.
divination.explanation: A near-term inflation forecast aligned with RBNZ guidance; plausible but subject to global price shocks.

divination.statement: I find it troubling when I'm misrepresented in this House. I did not say that. I said up to 130,000 families could benefit. You know what? We've got lots of years in office left to go, so I'm confident that might happen.
divination.explanation: 'I'm confident that might happen' is a hedged prediction of future uptake with uncertain basis.

divination.statement: From 2028, the Waikato medical school will train 120 new doctors every year, adding to our homegrown workforce. It uses a new graduate-entry model that brings in people with real-world experience and a broad range of backgrounds.
divination.explanation: Forecasts 120 doctors/year from 2028; plausible if the school proceeds as planned but dependent on delivery.
